mkdir -p /tmp/opensip-design-corrections/consumer-b.v5/output/work && /tmp/opensip-architecture-review-env/bin/python -I -B - <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, os
base="/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/consumer-b.v5/subject"
m=json.load(open(os.path.join(base,"consumer-input-manifest.json")))
ok=bad=0; results=[]
listed=set()
for f in m["files"]:
    p=os.path.join(base,f["path"]); listed.add(f["path"])
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        results.append((f["path"],"MISSING")); bad+=1; continue
    b=open(p,'rb').read()
    h=hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
    st = "OK" if (h==f["sha256"] and len(b)==f["bytes"]) else f"MISMATCH got={h} bytes={len(b)}"
    results.append((f["path"],st))
    ok+= (st=="OK"); bad+= (st!="OK")
onfs=set()
for root,d,fs in os.walk(base):
    for x in fs:
        rp=os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root,x),base)
        if rp!="consumer-input-manifest.json": onfs.add(rp)
print("verified OK:",ok,"bad:",bad)
for p,s in results:
    if s!="OK": print("  ",p,s)
print("extra files on disk not in manifest:", sorted(onfs-listed))
print("manifest entries missing on disk:", sorted(listed-onfs))
print("total files:",len(m["files"]))
PY

1	# OpenSIP product contracts
2	
3	This consolidated contract set describes the complete intended product selected
4	by D-371. Its current review and application standing is recorded in the
5	[correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md) and the
6	[central readiness register](../../architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md#unified-product-design-readiness).
7	These contract bytes alone grant no readiness grade or implementation authority.
8	
9	The product has one host for discovery, input admission, authority, orchestration,
10	evaluation, evidence storage and output. Language-specific analyzers contribute
11	facts and Coverage through versioned protocols. The evaluator is pure. An
12	invocation can compose analysis, queries, imports, policy changes, repair and
13	verification; only an authoritative analysis seals a source-bound Run.
14	
15	```mermaid
16	flowchart LR
17	  R[Repository and explicit inputs] --> H[Host discovery and admission]
18	  H --> I[Invocation and ordered steps]
19	  I --> N[Native analyzers]
20	  N --> F[Admitted facts and Coverage]
21	  F --> E[Pure policy evaluation]
22	  E --> V[Proof verification and immutable Run]
23	  V --> S[Evidence store and portable baseline]
24	  S --> O[CLI JSON SARIF HTML agent views]
25	  S --> P[Authorized repair preview and apply]
26	  P --> H
27	```
28	
29	Read the five contracts together:
30	
31	1. [Identity and evidence](identity-and-evidence.md): exact semantic identities,
32	   independent replay, durable defaults, retention, purge and recovery.
33	2. [Security and lifecycle](security-and-lifecycle.md): repository boundaries,
34	   time/trust recovery, revocation, supported platform profiles, migration and
35	   concurrent operations.
36	3. [Native evidence](native-evidence.md): TS/JS/Rust capability cells, sealed
37	   dependency/prepared inputs, resolution completeness and clone candidates.
38	4. [Workflows and surfaces](workflows-and-surfaces.md): invocations, baseline and
39	   changed-code audit, typed imports/comparison, policy/review/repair and output.
40	5. [Admission and qualification](admission-and-qualification.md): exact numeric
41	   parsing, independent report oracles and release measurement requirements.
42	
43	The Fallow-inspired behavior belongs in these contracts now, even where its
44	implementation is scheduled later. Zero-config discovery, stable output,
45	composed invocations, retained evidence, changed-code gating and advisory
46	boundaries apply across languages. Native syntax/resolution, clone normalization
47	and runtime-format adapters are deliberately language-specific.
48	
49	Historical contracts and preview reviews remain immutable evidence. They do
50	not provide an alternative current command grammar or a competing preview
51	product. The normative retained/superseded selector tables in these five
52	contracts determine the applicable design recipes; a current explicit successor
53	wins over the named inherited selector only within its declared scope. Any
54	unresolved overlap is a design defect, never reviewer discretion. The correction
55	crosswalk records the corresponding review/application evidence, and the central
56	readiness register remains the sole completion checklist. Those two governance
57	records grant standing; they are not additional semantic recipes and are omitted
58	from blind reconstruction inputs to avoid disclosing prior verdicts. Passing design reference checks is not product qualification.
59	
60	Current correction status and review blockers: [correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md).

2	
3	Standing: product successor authored by Codex, with review and application
4	standing governed by the [correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md)
5	and central readiness register. This is the Phase-1A packet for the intended
6	product, not a repair of the historical preview's acceptance record. The

11	## 1. Authority and applicability
12	
13	The host admits inputs, mints identities, evaluates policy through the pure
14	evaluator, verifies its result, and commits evidence. Native providers, imported
15	observations, model suggestions and stored caller-supplied identifiers do not
16	have evaluation or custody authority. Signed software provenance does not prove
17	that an algorithm is correct; the selected, authenticated first-party host and
18	pure evaluator remain in the TCB. No Python introspection guard or caller's
19	`verified=true` is an authority mechanism.
20	
21	This contract prospectively replaces the Run/evidence/Plan/source/view/finding/
22	proof/cache/regeneration recipes and their parks in freeze §7.1,
23	`evidence-identity-recipes.v5.json`, `evaluation-proof.v8.json`'s claim-shape
24	lineage and `evaluation-proof.v13.json`'s provenance lineage. Neither evaluation
25	candidate becomes retrospectively applied. It replaces the Phase-1A and
26	retention-result join missing from `evidence.v15.json`, and consumes the
27	CD-RT-5 posture implemented by `retention-tiers.v28.json`. It supplies the
28	identity-dependent parts of R-1, trusted-request context and OPERABILITY G19.
29	Precise residual dispositions and source pins are in the integration record.
30	
31	Unchanged inherited constraints: no ambient provider reads; sealed snapshot;
32	complete protocol transaction plus successful process exit and EOF before facts
33	are admitted; pure deterministic evaluation; one host writer; deny-by-absence
34	permissions; lifetime-neutral semantics. Existing relation payload schemas can
35	be referenced by exact digest. Their historical FactRecord1 wrapper cannot bind
36	a snapshot2 identifier; product FactRecord2 is an explicit successor.

38	## 2. Tenant and operational identity
39	
40	ProjectId retains PROJECT-ID-V1: `prj1-` followed by 64 lower-case hex digits,
41	32 host-CSPRNG bytes. The untracked `.opensip/project-id.v1` marker and the
42	private host registry must agree exactly. A private namespace UUID is an
43	operational storage locator, bound one-to-one to ProjectId; it does not enter
44	semantic identities. The host verifies marker, root identity, owner, no-follow
45	handles and registry binding before any project writer. Missing marker and
46	registry is first use; agreement is reuse; either unilateral or contradictory
47	presence is an admission refusal requiring explicit recovery/adoption. It never
48	silently chooses one identity. Discovery and admission use the security unit's
49	root boundary.
50	
51	An ordinary fresh clone gets a fresh ProjectId. Explicit adoption from an
52	admitted portable project bundle preserves a ProjectId after showing its source
53	and target; it never imports another machine's local authorization, credentials,
54	leases or execution receipts. A fork gets a new ProjectId and explicit origin
55	metadata. A root move preserves ProjectId only through an authenticated registry
56	move with no live writer; duplicate simultaneous roots for one local namespace
57	refuse. Read-only comparison of two tenants does not merge their stores.
58	
59	Invocation identity is RequestId (`req1_` plus 32 lower-case hex digits), minted
60	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. Each admitted
61	attempt receives a fresh ExecutionId (`exec1_` plus 32 lowercase hex digits).
62	`c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json` `planIntent.wireTypes.executionId` is the C-2
63	owner selector for EXECUTION-ID-V1 **provenance** — where the identifier and its
64	uniqueness discipline come from — and it is not byte-equivalent to the product
65	successor grammar. Its pattern ends in a bare `$`, so it admits
66	`exec1_<32 hex>\n`, which `admission-and-qualification` §1 declares malformed and
67	which `common.schema.json#/$defs/ExecutionId` refuses. The **product successor
68	grammar is end-anchored**: `^exec1_[0-9a-f]{32}(?![\s\S])`, exactly as
69	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/commit-receipt/properties/executionId` and the
70	workflow `ExecutionId` spell it, and a trailing newline, carriage return or space
71	is refused rather than trimmed. RequestId is `^req1_[0-9a-f]{32}(?![\s\S])` on the
72	same rule. This is the same deliberate non-equivalence security §S9.1 states for
73	`RootV1`: the retained selector remains the immutable provenance record, the
74	successor is what admits.
75	Both RequestId and ExecutionId use independent 16-byte host-CSPRNG draws, reserved
76	with uniqueness checked in the corresponding operational ledger before use.
77	Caller-supplied IDs and reuse are refused; neither is derived from a content hash.
78	This prospectively settles RES-C2V4-01 ownership in the shared identity contract.
79	StepId is the zero-based integer position in the invocation's ordered DAG.
80	Retry always receives a new ExecutionId. These identities, wall clocks, PIDs,
81	credentials, authorization nonces, receipts and output destinations are
82	operational and excluded from Run identity. Identical semantic inputs can
83	produce the same Run on two attempts; attempts remain separately auditable.

85	## 3. Exact canonical encoding and identity preimages
86	
87	The authoritative schema is `foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json` (closed
88	Draft 2020-12 records); semantic joins below are equally mandatory. JSON Schema
89	alone does not establish exact numeric admission. Before deserialization loses
90	lexical information, reject duplicate keys, floating/exponent tokens, `-0`,
91	nonfinite tokens, malformed UTF-8 and non-scalar Unicode. Integer range is
92	[-2^63, 2^64-1], booleans are distinct, and every field has its narrower schema
93	bound. Maximum descriptor is 4 MiB and nesting depth 32: the root container
94	counts as 1; scalar leaves and object keys add no container depth. Byte inventories may
95	name larger independently bounded blobs. A descriptor exceeding a bound is
96	rejected; it is never truncated into a different identity.
97	
98	Canonical JSON has UTF-8 byte-ordered keys, no whitespace or trailing newline,
99	no Unicode normalization, shortest ordinary decimal integers, and unescaped
100	Unicode scalar characters. Escape quote and backslash, use `\b\t\n\f\r`, and
101	lowercase `\u00xx` for other U+0000–001F controls; do not escape slash. Arrays are encoded **in their admitted order**: C never sorts, deduplicates or
102	infers semantics from a field name or `uniqueItems`. The closing default for
103	any array in a registered payload is an **ordered sequence**, including nested
104	arrays and raw token arrays. A schema/owning contract may prescribe a stricter
105	order; its producer constructs that order and admission refuses deviations
106	before hashing. This separation applies to every auxiliary digest as well as H.
107	
108	`x-opensip-order` is the machine-readable schema annotation for these orders, and
109	the closed vocabulary is exactly the one the `x-opensip-order` validator keyword in
110	`foundation/canonical.py` implements: `sequence` (default); `canonical-set` (strict
111	ascending canonical item bytes); `canonical-order` (nondecreasing canonical item
112	bytes, repeats allowed); `utf8` (strict ascending UTF-8 bytes of a scalar string
113	item); `path` (strict ascending UTF-8 `path`); `numeric` (strict ascending
114	integers); `ordinal` (contiguous zero-based `ordinal`); `predicate` (strict
115	ascending UTF-8 `ruleId,subjectId,predicateId` tuple); `ruleId` and `waiverId`
116	(strict ascending UTF-8 value of that key); and the generic object form
117	`{"by": [key, ...]}` (strict ascending UTF-8 tuple of those item keys, in the
118	listed order). All except `sequence` and `canonical-order` also require unique sort
119	keys; `uniqueItems` alone neither selects nor overrides an order. An annotation
120	outside this vocabulary refuses rather than passing silently. Explicit owning
121	schema/contract order takes precedence over the sequence default and must agree
122	with any annotation. No caller may elect a different order for one schema.
123	
124	Every array in identity-schemas.v2 carries this annotation: semantic collections
125	use `canonical-set`, inventories use `path`, dependencies use `numeric`, stages
126	use `ordinal` and predicate proofs use `predicate`. Inventory paths must be
127	unique even when two rows have different byte digests or lengths; there is no
128	tie-break, and duplicate paths refuse before an identity is minted. Configuration
129	`allowedScopes` preserves declared priority; declaration-signature tokens
130	preserve grammar order, including repeated tokens. PolicyDocumentV1 and
131	RuleProgramV1 `rules` preserve their schema's `ruleId` order, never canonical
132	rule-object order; WaiverSetV1 uses `waiverId`. Other native/workflow arrays
133	preserve their admitted sequence subject to their explicitly declared ordering
134	rules. This settles all arrays without an implicit set heuristic.
135	
136	Text maxLength counts Unicode scalar values, while the descriptor byte cap
137	remains independent. U+007F and U+2028 remain unescaped. Logical
138	paths are relative slash-separated scalar strings, without empty, dot, dot-dot,
139	NUL or backslash segments. Source spans are half-open byte offsets, bounded by
140	the exact named source blob; they never split UTF-8 characters in text anchors.
141	Native language identifiers may have their own explicit normalization; that is
142	a payload property, never an implicit change to this canonical encoder.
143	
144	For domain D and descriptor X:
145	
146	`H(D,X) = SHA256(ASCII("opensip.product.v1") || 00 || ASCII(D) || 00 || uint64BE(length(C(X))) || C(X))`.
147	
148	The identifier is the prefix below, a colon, and lowercase H hex. A raw blob
149	reference uses SHA256 of its exact bytes and its byte length. A semantic
150	reference must name its domain, not just an untyped hash. No path, display
151	version or claimed digest substitutes for verified bytes.

343	### The closing digest law
344	
345	Arrays have a closing default; so do digests. **Every 64-hex field in
346	identity-schemas.v2 has exactly one representation and one retention mode**,
347	declared field-by-field by the machine-readable `x-opensip-digest` schema
348	annotation. There is no residue: a 64-hex field carrying no annotation is
349	inadmissible, and a producer may not choose a representation for it. Nothing in
350	this graph infers a digest's meaning from a **field name**: a `Digest` spelling,
351	a `sha256` key or a bare hex string carries no meaning by itself, and two fields
352	with the same name have the same recipe only because the annotation says so.
353	The array law closes by naming a default; this law closes by admitting **no**
354	default, which is stronger: a new 64-hex field added without an annotation
355	refuses at admission instead of silently inheriting a plausible rule, so the
356	omission that produced this paragraph cannot recur unnoticed.
357	
358	The four representations are closed:
359	
360	| Representation | Meaning |
361	|---|---|
362	| `raw-artifact` | raw SHA256 of the **exact retained artifact bytes** — a source or closure-tree file, a committed capability-manifest artifact, a component manifest body, or a complete registered schema document. Not of a canonicalization of anything. |
363	| `canonical-record` | raw SHA256 of `C(record)` for a **named registered record**. The annotation names it: a `#/$defs/…` record of this bundle, a `{document, selector}` record registered by another unit's pinned schema, a record `registeredBy` a sibling schema-document digest, or the workflow `PayloadRegistryV1` row keyed by an import's `kind` and `payloadDomain`. |
364	| `h-identity` | the lowercase hex of `H(D, X)` — either a typed object of a domain in the table above, carried with its prefix, or the **bare 64-hex suffix** of a domain in a named domain set. Never raw SHA256 of the payload. |
365	| `capability-manifest-id` | the inherited CVE1 recipe `SHA256(UTF8("opensip.capability-manifest.v1") ‖ 00 ‖ committedBytes)`, closed to `plan.capabilityManifestId`, `run.capabilityManifestId` and the `capability-manifest` reference domain. |
366	
367	The four retention modes are closed:
368	
369	| Retention | Meaning |
370	|---|---|
371	| `preimage` (default) | the exact preimage bytes are retained in the content-addressed store **under this digest**; the closure checker fetches them and re-hashes. |
372	| `fragment` | the preimage is a canonical sub-object of an already retained record; the annotation's `locatedBy` states which record and which addressing rule, and the closure checker recomputes it there rather than storing it twice. Closed to `program-predicate.nodeDigest`. |
373	| `derived` | recomputed from another retained artifact by the stated recipe. Closed to `capabilityManifestId`, derived from the `capabilityManifestBytesDigest` artifact. |
374	| `owner-retained` | the named owning contract retains and admits the bytes; this closure joins by digest equality only. Closed to `owner-source-set[].ownerFileManifestSha256`, owned by security's `RepoExecutionGrantV2` owner admission. |
375	
376	Because `H(D, X)` is `SHA256` of the framed preimage, **one** content-addressed
377	store keyed by raw SHA256 retains all three of raw artifacts, canonical records
378	and H identities: the object retained under a bare-hex `h-identity` digest is the
379	exact H preimage frame
380	`ASCII("opensip.product.v1") ‖ 00 ‖ ASCII(D) ‖ 00 ‖ uint64BE(length(C(X))) ‖ C(X)`.
381	Frame admission is exact and is not a blob escape: the literal prefix must match,
382	the domain must be a member of the annotation's named domain set, the declared
383	length must equal the remaining byte count, the remainder must be byte-identical
384	to `C` of its own parse, and the parsed payload must validate under the record
385	that the domain set registers for that domain. A frame is admissible **only**
386	where the annotation says `h-identity`; conversely a raw canonical payload is
387	never admissible there, because `C(X)` does not begin with the framing prefix and
388	`SHA256(C(X))` is not `H(D, X)`. A native `sha256:`-prefixed identity and a Plan's
389	bare-hex suffix are two spellings of one H digest and can never become a raw
390	payload SHA256, in either direction. Offering a frame where a `canonical-record`
391	is required fails parsing; offering a payload where a frame is required fails the
392	prefix.
393	
394	Two things are easy to conflate here, so they are separated explicitly. The
395	**annotation** is what closes a field: it says which representation and retention
396	that one field has. A **spelling** — a bare 64-hex string, a `sha256:` prefix, a
397	`fact2:`/`plan2:` typed prefix — is not an annotation and never implies one. This
398	contract does not claim that every prefixed identity in the graph carries the same
399	annotation, and no reader should infer that from the prefix: a typed prefix tells
400	you which domain *table* interprets the value, while the field's own annotation
401	tells you what the value *is*. Where a field carries the bare 64-hex suffix of an
402	`h-identity`, the annotation must name the **domain set** that resolves it,
403	because the suffix alone does not.
404	
405	`plan.nativeContextDigests` is exactly this case, and it is a **set**. A Plan may
406	name several admitted native contexts, including **several of the same language** —
407	two TypeScript projects under one Plan is ordinary, not exceptional. Nothing
408	elects one of them by position, by display order or by any other scalar. A fact's
409	`sourceUniverse` is an `h-identity` of a semantic-universe domain, and that
410	universe record names **its own** `nativeContextId`; that is what selects the
411	corresponding context, and the closure requires the selected context to be one the
412	Plan committed to. There is no arbitrary scalar display anywhere in that
413	selection.
414	
415	Reference `digest` fields (`Ref`, `ProofInputRef`, `FindingEvidenceRef`) take
416	their representation from their sibling `domain` through the normative
417	`x-opensip-digest-domains.byDomain` registry in identity-schemas.v2. Every member
418	of every `domain` enum is registered; an unregistered domain refuses. The
419	`coverage-payload`, `import-payload` and `fact-payload` reference domains are
420	resolved through the owning Coverage, import or fact object's
421	`payloadSchemaDigest`; they are not authoritative roots and the proof input
422	vocabulary excludes them.
423	
424	Auxiliary digests therefore have producing rules, not caller-defined meanings:
425	`resolvedConfigDigest` is SHA256 of the configuration resolver's canonical
426	semantic value (§1.1 of admission-and-qualification). `scopeDigest` hashes the
427	closed scope-descriptor record in identity-schemas.v2 (workspace roots, requested
428	path prefixes and excluded path prefixes, canonical sets of admitted relative
429	paths; `.` alone denotes the admitted project root, and every other path
430	is a strict logical path with no dot/parent/empty segment). `analysisSpecDigest` hashes the closed analysis-spec record (exact
431	registered capability/language-mode/workspace/required selections, policy pack
432	IDs and schema-bound parameter payloads). `semanticGrantDigest` hashes the
433	closed semantic-grant record: ProjectId, selected first-party or explicitly
434	trusted-repository principals and their exact closure/owner-source binding,
435	analysis operation set and scope. First-party principals have null owner source;
436	repository principals require the admitted owner-source digest. The projection
437	includes only read-source/read-import/native-analysis/prepare-code operations
438	actually needed by the analysis. Operational preparation grants are admitted
439	before a Plan exists; when analysis consumes their host-prepared outputs, its
440	projection must match the exact admitted preparation records retained with those
441	outputs under security's Plan-time join. A test-execution step has no Plan:
442	its runner/argv/snapshot authorization stays operational, and its observations
443	enter an analysis only through an admitted import2 with its execution provenance.
444	`test-code` is not an analysis semantic-grant operation. Storage, rendering and repair effect authority stays in the
445	operational request; it cannot be fabricated by this projection. Any absent
446	required permission refuses before Plan construction. Nonces, expiry, signing
447	receipts and local executable paths are not fields in the semantic projection.
448	
449	`vcsDigest` hashes the closed `vcs-observation` record: schemaVersion 2,
450	kind none/git/hg/svn/jj, commitId (null exactly for none), dirty, and
451	sourceInventoryDigest (raw SHA256 of the canonical source inventory, retained
452	as a blob). This is source provenance; it alone never authenticates imported
453	runtime-to-source correspondence.
454	
455	The closure checker parses and exactly validates scope, semantic configuration,
456	analysis specification, semantic grant, owner-source set, source inventory, VCS
457	observation, stage specs, finding parameters, predicate witnesses and program
458	predicates, and admits the policy document, resolved waiver set, compiled rule
459	program, import correspondence, build identity and observation through their
460	owning unit's schema admission. It dispatches on the `x-opensip-digest`
461	annotation of the field it is walking, never on that field's name, and refuses a
462	64-hex field the schema does not annotate.
463	The grant ProjectId/scope must join the Run/Plan. Witness program bytes must be
464	retained; matching facts and coverage must come from its explicitly named input
465	views. Predicate input refs are a subset of evaluationInputRefs; evidence view
466	roots equal the named views and coverage roots equal their coverage union.
467	Every visited fact/scope and view/proof/execution/evidence/seal joins the current
468	source or Plan, including objects reached through typed Ref fields. Proof/finding
469	Ref domains exclude Run, evidence, seal and proof outputs. The native and workflow
470	registered payload adapters are separate trusted admission stages, not assumed
471	validated merely because an opaque digest exists. The finite reference fixture
472	carries a real PolicyDocumentV1 and its compiled RuleProgramV1 in the product DSL,
473	so the record shapes, digests and joins above are exercised as specified; only its
474	*interpreter* is small, evaluating a single-atom subset, and it qualifies neither
475	the declarative language nor a native Coverage or relation payload registry.
476	
477	Import mapping/observation, correspondence, build identity, policy, rule-program
478	and waiver-set digests are `canonical-record` digests under their owning
479	workflow schema, named exactly by the annotation and admitted by that unit's own
480	schema admission, so there is one implementation of each record law and no second
481	policy or compiler language in this contract. `plan.policyDigest` and
482	`policy-derivation.policyDigest` name `PolicyDocumentV1`; `plan.waiverDigest` and
483	`policy-derivation.waiverDigest` name the resolved effective `WaiverSetV1`;
484	`proof.ruleProgramDigest` names `RuleProgramV1`. The compiled program is not a
485	free artifact: its `policyDigest` must equal the Plan's, and it must be exactly
486	the projection of the Plan-selected policy's rules
487	(`{schemaVersion:1, policyDigest, rules:[{ruleId, ruleProgramRef, emitWhen}]}`,
488	in the policy's own `ruleId` order). Blob bytes are `raw-artifact`. The source
489	inventory is the registered `source-inventory` record, and
490	`vcs-observation.sourceInventoryDigest` must equal the digest of the snapshot's

495	### The payload registry
496	
497	An earlier draft of this section additionally required "a document offered as a
498	*payload* schema must constrain the payload directly, so a multi-record bundle
499	cannot pass vacuously". **That requirement is withdrawn.** It contradicted the
500	native and workflow registries, which correctly hash the *exact full schema
501	document bytes* and validate through a registered **selector**; under the
502	withdrawn rule their own bundles were non-conforming, and no registry row named
503	a single-record document to replace them. The bundles were right and the sentence
504	was wrong.
505	
506	What replaces it is the thing that was actually missing: a closed registry saying,
507	for each payload, exactly which document bytes are hashed and which selector
508	validates. `identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-payload-registry` is that
509	registry. For every class in it:
510	
511	- `payloadSchemaDigest` is the **raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of the
512	  document the row names** — never a canonicalization of a selected `$def`;
513	- admission validates the payload against the row's **selector**, resolved through
514	  the pinned local closure with no network retrieval, so a multi-record bundle is
515	  admitted through its row and never needs a root type;
516	- the codec is `C`;
517	- a key with no row **refuses**. There is no default row, no caller-selected
518	  schema and no inferred one. A key name prefixed `payload.` is read from the
519	  parsed payload; every other name is read from the naming record.
520	
521	| Class | Keyed by | Document and selector |
522	|---|---|---|
523	| `relation` | `fact.relation` | `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json`, selector from that document's own `x-opensip-relation-registry` row |
524	| `coverage` | `payload.schemaVersion` | `native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/CoverageResultV3` |
525	| `import` | `import.kind` + `payload.payloadDomain` | the workflow `PayloadRegistryV1` / native §7.1 rows, mirrored; Run closure re-derives them from the workflow registry and refuses on drift, so the two cannot diverge |
526	| `parameter` | the cited `schemaDigest` | a document on the closed list: `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json`, and `workflows/schemas/policy-document.schema.json#/$defs/ScopeDocumentV1` |
527	
528	`view.schemaDigests` names the registered documents a view admitted, and each
529	member must be one of them.
530	
531	**The `ScopeDocumentV1` parameter row (CB3-MUST-4).** The comparison contract
532	states that `EvaluationContext.scopeDigest` is the workflow glob scope-policy
533	document "bound as an analysis-spec parameter", and the `parameter` class was
534	closed to a single document. A key with no row refuses — there is no default row
535	and no caller-selected schema — so that binding refused at Plan admission and
536	the comparison scope axis (E2 to E3) could not be populated at all: one contract
537	required a binding a sibling contract's closed registry forbade. The row is
538	registered rather than the mechanism abandoned, because the scope policy is a
539	genuine Plan input and the parameter class is where Plan inputs are admitted.
540	
541	It is deliberately a **different record** from the foundation `scope-descriptor`
542	that `plan.scopeDigest` names, and neither substitutes for the other:
543	`scope-descriptor` is the repository extent actually walked (workspace roots and
544	path prefixes), `ScopeDocumentV1` is the policy's include/exclude glob selection
545	over that extent. Both may appear in one Plan. Because the class is keyed by the
546	cited **document** digest, two rows selecting different records out of one
547	document would be indistinguishable and the first listed would silently win;
548	that is the arbitrary selection the registry law forbids, so an ambiguous key
549	refuses. The class remains closed: a real but unregistered document, and a
550	caller-chosen permissive one, both still refuse.
551	
552	The bounded limitation is **accounted rather than lifted**. Today's two rows are
553	distinguishable — `import-source-context.schema.json` and
554	`policy-document.schema.json` are different documents with different digests — so
555	nothing is ambiguous in this release, and the same `policy-document.schema.json`
556	bytes named by `plan.policyDigest` and `plan.waiverDigest` sit under the
557	`canonical-record` representation in a *different* payload class, outside this
558	key space entirely. What the key forbids is a **future** second `parameter` row
559	selecting another `$def` out of a document an existing row already cites; that is
560	a refusal (`PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW`), not a defect, and it is the
561	registry declining to choose arbitrarily. Re-keying the class by
562	`(document, selector)` would remove the restriction and would change no identity
563	today — and is deliberately not done, because no requirement needs such a row,
564	and widening a closed key space and retiring an explicit refusal for a case that
565	does not exist buys flexibility nothing asked for. If that requirement ever
566	arises it is an explicit versioned correction with its own controls, never a
567	silent widening and never something an implementer may assume.
568	
569	**Where the binding is actually decided, and where it is only asserted.**
570	Registering the row makes a lawful scope parameter admissible at Plan closure;
571	it does not by itself bind the *comparison* context to it. `adopt_baseline`
572	assigns `context.scopeDigest` from the scope document it is **passed**, and its
573	`plan` argument is a PlanId **string** — so that assignment records the digest
574	of whatever document the caller supplied and is **not** evidence that the
575	document was the Run's selected analysis-spec parameter. The same holds for
576	`policyDigest` and `waiverSetDigest`. Calling that assignment a binding would be
577	false, and this contract does not.
578	
579	The honest boundary is therefore stated rather than implied. `adopt_baseline` is
580	a **pure projection over documents the caller must already have admitted**, and
581	its precondition is exactly that `policy`, `scope` and `waivers` are the
582	documents the Plan selected. Selection membership is decidable only with the
583	retained analysis-spec record in hand, so a bounded verifier takes that record
584	and proves it: the scope document's canonical digest must be the `payloadDigest`
585	of a selected parameter row citing the registered `ScopeDocumentV1` **document**
586	digest. A document that is not selected, a spec that selects no scope parameter,
587	and a row cited under another schema each refuse with their own typed reason.
588	When the analysis spec is supplied, `adopt_baseline` performs that verification;
589	when it is not, the scope binding is a **caller assertion** and this contract
590	says so rather than implying a join. Neither path changes the baseline
591	descriptor or its identity, and no product host is implied here.
592	
593	The two scope records remain different things throughout: the foundation
594	`scope-descriptor` that `plan.scopeDigest` names is the repository extent
595	actually walked, while `ScopeDocumentV1` is the operator's include/exclude glob
596	policy over that extent.

598	### `fact2` payload encoding: one explicit successor law
599	
600	The inherited `fact-plane.v1.json`
601	`$.factRecordContractV1.relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.canonicalPayloadEncoding`
602	is a deterministic-CBOR profile that forbids negative integers and non-NFC text,
603	while `fact2.payloadDigest` is a `canonical-record` digest under `C`, which admits
604	both. Two owning statements in direct contradiction is a design defect, so this
605	contract settles it in one direction and says exactly what changes.
606	
607	**`fact2` payloads are `C`.** There is one product encoder and no second codec in
608	the trusted computing base. Every *logical* restriction the CBOR profile carried
609	survives, as an admission rule expressed in the registered schema rather than
610	implied by a codec: NFC-only text, no negative integers, `uint64` range, the
611	closed field set, the enums, the per-rung required/forbidden fields and the
612	`universeRule`. `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json` carries all
613	thirteen relations — the twelve inherited from fact-plane plus native §4.4's
614	`unresolved-edge` — reproducing each inherited `required`, `optional`, field type
615	and enum exactly, and its `x-opensip-relation-registry` carries each relation's
616	selector, universe rule and rung ladder.
617	
618	**The ladder is an explicit array, and `rungs` is not it (CB3-MUST-1).** That
619	registry had no `ladder` key at all. Its `rungs` member is a per-rung
620	required/forbidden **field-rule** table, and it is legitimately the empty object
621	for a relation with no per-rung field variance — which is every single-rung
622	relation: `file`, `package`, `vcs-change`, `declares`, `literal`,
623	`control-flow`, `reachability` and `clones`. Reading `rungs` as the ladder gives
624	two conforming readings and both are wrong: read strictly, those eight relations
625	admit no `resolution` at all and no Run of the kind these contracts require
626	could close; read leniently — as the reference closure did, via an
627	`and row['rungs']` guard — the ladder check is skipped entirely for them, and a
628	`declares` fact carrying `resolved-callee`, a rung of `calls`, closes a Run.
629	The rung vocabulary is shared across relations, so such a value is perfectly
630	well-formed; **schema vocabulary is not relation membership.**
631	
632	Each row therefore carries an explicit ordered **`ladder`**, weakest-first,
633	inherited verbatim from `fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry.relations[].ladder` plus
634	`[observed]` for `unresolved-edge`. This registry is the **single authority**;
635	`native_evidence_model.v2.LADDERS` and
636	`capability-manifest-domains.v2 RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders` are declared
637	mirrors of it and are drift-checked **exactly and in order**. Order is not
638	decoration: the capability registry's arrays had been alphabetised while still
639	naming the inherited ladder as their source, which reversed `calls`, `imports`
640	and `references` — harmless only because that registry is consulted for
641	membership alone, and an inversion for anything that read it as an order.
642	
643	Membership is decided against `ladder`, always, with **no empty-ladder
644	fallback**: a relation with no ladder is a registry defect and refuses rather
645	than admitting anything. Order comparison is the index within one relation's
646	own ladder. Nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another,
647	and there is no global rank; a cross-relation comparison is an admission
648	refusal, never a true or false predicate.
649	
650	**One rung vocabulary, named directly (CB3-MUST-2).** The policy DSL previously
651	carried its own abstract tier vocabulary — `syntax`, `resolved`, `type`,
652	`external` — reached from `PolicyDocumentV1` `Atom.minResolution` and reused by
653	repair's `EvidenceRequirement`. It shared **zero** members with the fifteen rung
654	names every fact, Coverage entry and native `RequirementV2` actually carries, no
655	document mapped one onto the other, and the evaluator compared them through a
656	single global rank table (`{syntax:0, resolved:1, type:2, external:1}`) shared by
657	every relation. Whether `minResolution: resolved` was satisfied by
658	`resolved-target`, by `resolved-binding`, by `checked` or by all three is a
659	public semantic decision, so two conforming implementations emitted different
660	findings from the same Plan.
661	
662	Preserving the abstract syntax with a published mapping was considered and
663	rejected. Such a mapping must be **per relation** — `resolved` names a different
664	rung in each of `imports`, `references`, `calls` and `reachability`, `type`
665	names a rung only for `types`, and `external` names no native rung at all — so
666	it is a partial, lossy renaming with no expressive power, and it does not even
667	preserve the one-word-one-meaning property that motivates an abstract syntax. It
668	also cannot survive C-1: `syntax < resolved < type` **is** a global ladder, and
669	making it relation-relative dissolves it into the rung names. The smaller and
670	coherent correction is to name the rung: `Atom.minResolution` and
671	`EvidenceRequirement.minResolution` are rung names, the abstract `Resolution`
672	enum and the global `RES_ORDER` rank are **withdrawn**, and satisfaction is
673	ladder-index comparison inside one relation.
674	
675	Two admission conditions follow, because no schema keyword can express the
676	second without restating the ladders and creating another independent source.
677	The schema constrains `minResolution` to the flat rung vocabulary — exactly the
678	union of the registry's ladders, drift-checked — which is **necessary**.
679	Membership of *this atom's relation's* ladder is **sufficient** and is enforced
680	at admission: in the workflow policy resolver, and at the **Run closure**, over
681	both the Plan's `PolicyDocumentV1` and the proof's compiled `RuleProgramV1`. An
682	evaluator-only check would let a sealed Run assert a predicate that was never
683	admissible. Atom relations are closed too: an atom names either one of the
684	thirteen native fact relations or one of the imported-evidence relations closed
685	by `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry`
686	(`runtime-observation`, `history-change`, each with the one-rung ladder
687	`[observed]` — no new rung token), and an evidence relation must declare its
688	`evidence` kind while a native fact relation must not.
689	
690	**What does not change:** historical `FactRecord1` records, their CBOR wire bytes
691	and their provenance are untouched and remain valid history. They are never a
692	`fact2` preimage, and this contract has always said the historical wrapper cannot
693	bind a `snapshot2` identifier. **The conversion is stated, not delegated:** a
694	provider that emits deterministic CBOR has its payload decoded under the selected
695	registered schema and re-encoded to `C` by the trusted first-party host adapter
696	before `fact2` is minted; the adapter refuses rather than repairs a payload that
697	violates any retained restriction, and persistence stores the `C` bytes that
698	`payloadDigest` names. No unspecified adapter invents a schema.
699	
700	Joined at Run closure for every fact: the relation must be registered;
701	`payloadSchemaDigest` must be the relation document's own file digest;
702	`resolution` must be a rung of that relation's ladder; that rung's required and
703	forbidden fields must hold; and `universeRule: same-only` requires
704	`sourceUniverse == targetUniverse`.
705	
706	#### Relation payloads: the digest law, and what a payload's claim is joined to
707	
708	The closing digest law above governs identity-schemas.v2, and the native contract
709	extends it to its own bundle. `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json` was
710	governed by **neither**, so its digest-bearing and path-bearing fields carried no
711	annotation and a `file` payload's `path`, `contentSha256` and `byteLength` were
712	joined to nothing at all: a schema-valid fact could claim any content hash for
713	any path, including a path in no snapshot, and close a Run. That was a real
714	defect and this is its closure, as a class rather than as one field.
715	
716	That document now carries its own `x-opensip-digest-law`, and **every**
717	`DigestHex`, `Sha256Text` and `CanonicalPath` field in it is annotated with its
718	representation, producing preimage or codec, retention and owning authority. The
719	law is **consumed, not declared**: every annotated field must be reachable from
720	its relation's registry joins or must declare `retention: not-joined` with its
721	reason, and every field a join names must exist in the selector. A newly
722	annotated field with no join refuses, so this omission cannot recur silently.
723	
724	The relation document's annotation law also governs schema structure. A governed
725	occurrence is a reference to `DigestHex`, `Sha256Text` or `CanonicalPath`, including
726	an intermediate local `$defs` alias, or an inline pattern exactly equal to one of
727	those definitions' patterns. Follow local references, nested `properties`,
728	`items`, `additionalProperties` and `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` branches when checking
729	these occurrences. Following local references must terminate even when a local
730	definition is cyclic. An annotation on the occurrence, its enclosing schema
731	path, or an intermediate alias applies to that occurrence. An annotation on
732	the terminal governed scalar definition does **not** provide a blanket default
733	for all references to that type. Directly annotated top-level selector
734	properties remain subject to retention and join checks even when their scalar
735	form is not one of these three.
736	
737	Every governed occurrence must have an effective annotation. An annotated
738	alternative does not cover an unannotated alternative; a parent annotation may
739	cover each alternative it encloses. When multiple schema paths reach the same
740	location, any occurrence lacking an effective annotation makes that location
741	inadmissible. Later annotated occurrences cannot undo that absence. Object-key
742	order and the order in which these paths are visited must not change admission.
743	
744	There is no precedence rule between disagreeing effective annotations at one
745	location: distinct annotations conflict and the document refuses; repeated
746	annotations that are equal under typed canonical equality do not conflict.
747	Every effective annotation must use the declared retention vocabulary. These
748	same effective annotations govern coverage, retention and join/exemption checks;
749	none of those checks may silently revert to inspecting only direct properties.
750	
751	The current registry's join fields address top-level selector properties.
752	Taking a scalar alternative of such a property preserves that address; entering
753	an object member, array element or map value does not. A governed occurrence at
754	one of those nested locations must explicitly declare `retention: not-joined`.

756	for a reader; admission checks the declared retention, not the presence or
757	content of that prose. It cannot claim a joinable retention that the current
758	join vocabulary cannot address. An addressable annotated property requires its
759	registry join unless it declares that exemption, and every named join field
760	must exist in the selector. Missing annotations, conflicting annotations,
761	undeclared retention values, unaddressable claimed joins, missing joins and
762	joins naming absent fields all refuse at schema-law admission. This check
763	establishes coherence of the registered schema; the owning-fact snapshot and
764	retained-byte joins below still establish the truth of each admitted payload.

766	`x-opensip-relation-registry` carries a normative per-relation **`snapshotJoins`**
767	table, and Run closure applies it to **every owning fact** — after the registered
768	selector validation, and **independently of the payload decode memo**, because
769	the truth of a claim about a snapshot is a property of the *owner*, not of the
770	bytes. A payload alone cannot decide it, so the closure requires owner context:
771	the enclosing fact, the snapshot **that fact names**, the retained blobs and the
772	bound native context. The four relations that make such a claim:
773	
774	| Relation | Join |
775	|---|---|
776	| `file` | `path` must be in the enclosing fact's snapshot source inventory; `contentSha256` must equal that inventory row's digest; `byteLength` must equal its length; the bytes must be **retained** under that digest and re-hash to it; and every anchor of the fact must lie in the very file the payload claims. |
777	| `package` | `manifestPath` must be in that inventory. |
778	| `vcs-change` | `path` must be in that inventory **unless** `changeKind` is `deleted`, where the path is by definition absent from the analysed snapshot. |
779	| `clones` | the framed body-identity join below. |

781	**How many anchors a fact carries is decided per relation, and the inventory
782	class carries none.** `fact.anchors` has no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever
783	stated a cardinality, so both the `file` row's every-anchor clause above and
784	native §1.2's every-anchor-path rule are universally quantified over an array of
785	unstated length — *vacuously true* at zero anchors, permitting and forbidding
786	nothing. Both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim consequently closed a Run
787	with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a closed
788	`anchorLaw` on every relation:
789	
790	| Class | Relations | Anchors | Why |
791	|---|---|---|---|
792	| `source-text` | `declares`, `literal`, `control-flow`, `imports`, `references`, `calls`, `types`, `reachability`, `unresolved-edge` | **≥ 1** | The fact was read from source text; an unanchored one names no file that could have been read. No *additional relation-specific* maximum and no canonical extent beyond the common schema bounds (`fact.anchors` keeps its `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`): which spans a producer cites is a real statement about what it read, so differing citations are *different* semantic descriptors and no cross-provider identity is promised. |
793	| `body-identity` | `clones` | **= 1** | Exactly the body span the identity is over (unchanged). |
794	| `inventory` | `file`, `package`, `vcs-change` | **= 0** | The claim's whole semantic input is the payload, already bound to the snapshot by the joins in this table. An anchor could only restate part of an already-joined claim on an axis nothing derives — one semantic input, several spellings, several identities. |

796	Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can satisfy: a path
797	no bundled grammar reads, an extensionless path, and a `vcs-change` on a
798	`deleted` path, which the row above places outside the snapshot entirely and
799	which therefore cannot bear an anchor at all.

801	**The raw-byte boundary.** An inventory claim retains its path, content digest
802	and byte length **without anyone decoding the bytes**. With the class at zero
803	anchors the `ANCHOR_SOURCE` / `ANCHOR_RANGE` / `ANCHOR_UTF8` checks never run for
804	such a fact — they iterate the anchors — while the `inventoried-file` join above
805	still does, and it only hashes and measures. An **empty** file and a **non-UTF8
806	binary** file are therefore ordinary inventory, at an extensionless path as
807	readily as any other, and requiring bytes to parse as code or as UTF-8 merely to
808	record their path and hash would be a narrowing this contract never intended.
809	The code-span laws keep exactly the scope they had: the *same* non-UTF8 bytes
810	still refuse as a `source-text` anchor (`ANCHOR_UTF8`), and the digest, length
811	and path joins still refuse a wrong claim about those bytes.

814	Nothing reads `fact.anchors` as a finding location, so removing them removes no
815	route and no new flexibility is added. A finding locates through

818	`finding`, `finding-fingerprint`, `proof-bundle` and `predicate-witness` carry no

823	universe; and `anchorPathField` sat only on the `file` row, so a `package`

828	`vcs-change.previousPath` is the one declared exemption. A pre-rename path names
829	a state **before** the analysed snapshot; it is a historical observation, not a
830	current source claim, and joining it to this snapshot's inventory would refuse
831	every honest rename. The exemption is recorded as `retention: not-joined` with
832	that reason rather than left as residue, so the distinction between a current
833	source claim and a historical path observation is explicit in both directions.

835	An inventory row is a claim *about* bytes; retention is custody *of* them. A
836	`file` fact whose inventory row agrees but whose bytes are not retained is

867	  `levelVersion`, so the inherited frame bytes and field grammar are unchanged.

896	  that owns this body's path, from native §2.1's committed

1110	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
1111	
1112	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
1113	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
1114	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,
1115	relation/rung, typed field filter, quantifier, deterministic work bound and
1116	emission condition for each predicate. Query planning is an optimization only:
1117	a retained full-scan reference must agree on selected facts. Neither a provider
1118	nor a witness supplies its own expected result or filter. All consumed data are
1119	listed in the proof's evaluationInputRefs; no hidden lookup is allowed.
1120	
1121	A predicate proof binds rule, subject, predicate, operation, admitted inputs,
1122	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains
1123	schemaVersion=2, program predicate digest, sorted matching fact IDs, sorted
1124	Coverage IDs, optional integer count limit and sorted child-predicate IDs.
1125	The program predicate digest is the §3 `program-predicate` record, which addresses
1126	the exact node of the admitted rule program this proof discharges; the predicate
1127	ID and the child predicate IDs are that section's node addresses, not free
1128	labels. An atomic witness names no children; boolean witnesses name only earlier
1129	nodes in the same subject/rule DAG, and each named child must itself be proven
1130	for the same rule and subject. Predicate IDs are unique and the DAG is bounded
1131	by the rule program's admitted work bound. Witness facts must be exactly those
1132	selected by the program over the complete admitted view, not merely a subset
1133	chosen by the producer. Counts count distinct selected fact IDs. The verifier
1134	recomputes scope membership, matches, completeness and each result, and then
1135	recomputes finding fingerprints, findings, rule outcomes and aggregate verdict.
1136	Missing witness bytes is retention loss, not a false predicate.
1137	
1138	| Predicate | Positive/complete case | Incomplete case |
1139	|---|---|---|
1140	| exists | true on a matching fact; false only on complete absence | true on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1141	| none | false on a known match; true only on complete absence | false on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1142	| count-at-most N | false once more than N distinct matches exist; true when complete count ≤ N | false above N, otherwise indeterminate |
1143	| all-covered | true only with admitted resolution-complete coverage for the requested universe/rung | indeterminate |
1144	| and / or / not | strong Kleene three-valued logic; false dominates and, true dominates or | unresolved value propagates unless dominated |
1145	
1146	Completeness means the native contract's examined partition **and** resolution
1147	and closed-world requirements. An unresolved `m[k]()` can never establish
1148	no-consumer merely because the enumerator visited all subjects. Runtime unhit
1149	observations never supply universal static completeness. A rule expression that
1150	is true produces its declared outcome; findings arise only from the program's
1151	emission condition. A false condition is a retained no-match proof. An
1152	indeterminate required predicate is retained with typed deficiency. A schema,
1153	identity or interpreter fault is an operational failure, not a fourth logical
1154	truth value and not an authoritative Run. Aggregate policy fail dominates

1155	indeterminate, which dominates pass; a required operational fault has D9's
1156	operational precedence even if other steps have committed failing Runs.
1157	
1158	Before sealing, the host independently replays the admitted deterministic
1159	program against the retained closure and compares the complete normalized
1160	result (all predicate outcomes, omissions, findings and verdict), not just a
1161	checksum supplied by the producer. This verifier is first-party trusted code;
1162	this is reproducible verification, not a proof of mathematical soundness or a
1163	sandbox against a malicious host. Semantic conformance uses independent
1164	oracles and mutation cases. The exact evaluator executable, declarative program,
1165	input closure and witness bytes are retained, so an independent installation
1166	can replay without trusting the original result flags. No old Python route
1167	region is executed to decide product authority.
1168	
1169	Verification reads retained objects and creates an operational verification
1170	receipt. Regeneration executes the exact retained producer and Plan input
1171	closure into a candidate namespace, verifies each expected semantic identity,
1172	and publishes recovered availability only if all required bytes agree. A
1173	mismatch is an operational regeneration verification refusal: `HOST.IO_FAILURE`
1174	(class `operational-failed`, faultCause `host-io`, exit4), domain detail
1175	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch`. It cannot replace the sealed Run. New
1176	source or policy creates a new Plan/Run. Expired or
1177	revoked permission cannot be resurrected by a matching hash. A miss recomputes
1178	normally; a corrupt hit is quarantined and disclosed before any permitted retry.
1179	
1180	**Constructing a cache key and admitting a hit are two different acts, and only
1181	the second is an admission.** Key construction is pure and deterministic: exact
1182	schema admission and canonical order over the `cache-key` record, nothing more. It
1183	reads no bytes and resolves no reference, so a host may compute it before loading
1184	anything and miss cheaply; it is a lookup key and grants nothing. **Finding bytes
1185	under a matching key is not authority.** An entry may be consumed only against
1186	exactly the closure the Run itself requires: the stage spec retained and joined to
1187	this Plan, the producing closure retained and Plan-selected, every `scopeIds`
1188	member a retained `subject-scope` of this snapshot, the output schema document
1189	retained, and every `inputRefs` entry resolved through the same
1190	`x-opensip-digest-domains` registry the Run uses — so a consumed native context
1191	must be one this Plan selected, a consumed import must be one this Plan selected,
1192	and nothing is admitted under a guessed payload-domain schema. A bare
1193	`coverage-payload`, `import-payload` or `fact-payload` reference is refused as an
1194	authoritative root rather than resolved by guesswork; those are reached only
1195	through their owning object. A hit that clears all of this is reusable producer
1196	output, never evidence authority, and it never replaces or re-seals a Run. The
1197	same record and the same admission apply to a regeneration key; only the H domain
1198	differs, and a regeneration whose result disagrees remains the
1199	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch` refusal above.

1201	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1202	
1203	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1204	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1205	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1206	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1207	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1208	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1209	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1210	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1211	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1212	
1213	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1214	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1215	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1216	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1217	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1218	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1219	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1220	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1221	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1222	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1223	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1224	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1225	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1226	
1227	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1228	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1229	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1230	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1231	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1232	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1233	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1234	
1235	Commit order:
1236	
1237	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1238	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1239	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1240	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1241	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1242	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1243	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1244	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1245	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1246	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1247	
1248	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1249	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1250	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1251	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1252	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1253	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1254	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1255	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1256	
1257	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1258	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1259	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1260	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1261	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1262	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1263	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1264	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1265	
1266	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1267	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1268	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1269	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1270	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1271	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1272	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1273	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1274	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1275	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete
1276	current `activePins` inventory sorted uniquely by `pinId`, and the three ordered
1277	consequences `named-pins-revoked`,
1278	`dependent-evidence-replay-unavailable`, `sealed-history-retained` — exactly as
1279	**workflows-and-surfaces §12** specifies. No pin is omitted, truncated or
1280	aggregated into a count. Neither that disclosure nor any flag confers authority:
1281	a later destructive attempt still requires the explicit lifecycle authorization
1282	and disclosure of its then-current complete pin set, and a changed pin inventory
1283	requires renewed disclosure before destruction. Purge retains the
1284	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
1285	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
1286	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
1287	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
1288	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
1289	
1290	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
1291	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
1292	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
1293	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
1294	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
1295	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
1296	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
1297	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
1298	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
1299	
1300	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
1301	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
1302	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
1303	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
1304	Source provenance/authenticity is reported separately from hash integrity.
1305	Trust floors, current authorization and local custody receipts are never
1306	restored backwards from an evidence backup. Portable baseline details are in
1307	the workflow contract. An import cannot silently claim a remote Run was locally
1308	evaluated: its imported-custody receipt names origin and local verification.

1310	## 6. Required implementation conformance
1311	
1312	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
1313	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
1314	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
1315	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
1316	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
1317	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
1318	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
1319	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
1320	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
1321	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
1322	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
1323	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
1324	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
1325	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
1326	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
1327	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
1328	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
1329	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
1330	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
1331	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
1332	closure. Their source pins
1333	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
1334	
1335	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
1336	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
1337	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
1338	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
1339	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
1340	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
1341	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.

1343	### Reference lifecycle joins
1344	
1345	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
1346	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
1347	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
1348	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
1349	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
1350	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
1351	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
1352	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
1353	
1354	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
1355	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
1356	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
1357	
1358	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
1359	
1360	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
1361	
1362	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). A label not in the expected set is wrong-build and cannot become a Plan-selected import. The schema bytes and payload are retained with the Plan parameters for independent replay.
1363	
1364	Snapshot capture consumes the same admitted boundary inventory as native discovery. The host obtains it from successful security discovery, passes it unchanged to native discovery/membership and the shared scope descriptor, and removes nested-repository, nested-project and directory-custody-excluded paths before opening or hashing snapshot source bytes. The remaining paths are only capture candidates: per-file custody, safe handles and exact hashing still precede source admission. Boundary exclusion anchors enter the Plan's scope descriptor and their operational provenance is retained beside it. The host reference join admits one inventory; caller-supplied alternative boundary lists or substituted marker sets are refused. Discovery's dependency-tree pruning is an analysis-unit rule; explicitly required native dependency read-set bytes require separate custody/closure admission and cannot cross a nested authority boundary.
1365	
1366	Every Plan with selected import2 inputs also requires read-import in its semantic grant. This includes imported-inert preparation. Close_run enforces this operation/input join as well as prepare-code/principal equality; the later consuming-Plan admission separately validates the actual preparedResolution provenance.
1367	
1368	
1369	The reference closure entry point reports a missing promised object/blob as EvidenceUnavailable carrying the closed operational-failed/HOST.IO_FAILURE/host-io termination with evidence.missing and the missing reference. It never emits a bare lookup error or turns missing witness bytes into a false predicate or admission rejection. This models the host's retained-byte/custody observation boundary. Untrusted malformed records still receive exact schema/identity admission refusal; an inventory of available retained bytes does not authorize rewriting the assurance of a sealed Run.

8	## 1. Numeric and schema admission

10	The configuration, policy and metadata carriers apply lexical admission before
11	JSON decoding can round or normalize a number. An integer field accepts an
12	ordinary integer token in its declared range. `1.0`, `1e0`, `1E0`,
13	`1.0000000000000001`, `9007199254740991.1`, booleans and numeric strings do not
14	satisfy an integer field, even if a JSON Schema implementation treats them as
15	mathematically equal. `-0`, nonfinite tokens and values outside the canonical
16	profile range are rejected. Internal configuration layers must also enforce
17	exact types; an already-decoded `1.0` or `True` cannot satisfy `const:1`.
18	
19	The [canonical reference](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/canonical.py)
20	provides duplicate-key, Unicode, depth, size and number admission plus an exact
21	integer/const/enum validator. Existing carrier-specific narrower bounds remain.
22	The new [foundation reference](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/host-foundation-model.v2.py)
23	replaces only the configuration/policy/parser entry points of
24	`completion/host-foundation-model.v1.py`. Root discovery belongs to the security
25	successor; no unsafe historical ancestor search is re-exported as current.
26	
27	Schema validation follows lexical admission and precedes configuration merge,
28	identity computation, subprocess disclosure or effects. Invalid external input
29	is an admission rejection with the existing carrier's D9 code; an invalid
30	host-generated internal layer is a host invariant fault. Unknown keys and
31	unsupported schema majors are refused. No parse fallback silently narrows a
32	user's configuration. UR-1–UR-5 are selected explicitly by the canonical profile
33	in identity-and-evidence §3, with byte vectors for non-BMP key ordering, integer
34	boundaries, Unicode normalization distinction, escaping and invalid surrogates.

36	Closed identifier and digest patterns require the actual end of the string.
37	The product schemas use the portable ECMAScript assertion `(?![\s\S])` where
38	an end anchor is intended, because `$` can also match before a final newline.
39	A newline-suffixed identifier or digest is malformed; stripping whitespace is
40	not an admission repair. Canonical string encoding itself continues to preserve
41	legal scalar characters, including escaped newlines in ordinary text fields.

170	## 2. Separate report custody, semantic correctness and qualification
171	
172	The release gate has an authenticated invocation context before reading a
173	candidate report: exact host, provider/data closure, harness, matrix, corpus,
174	runner public key, runner identity, environment observation and platform profile.
175	The fresh qualificationRequestId (host RequestId grammar) also binds the
176	measurement campaign; an older report cannot satisfy a different campaign.
177	These come from the selected signed release closure and independently admitted
178	runner inventory. A report cannot supply or alter its own expected subject,
179	expected answers, trusted runner or performance baseline.
180	
181	The producer signs the exact report bytes through the qualification signature
182	frame: ASCII `opensip.qualification.report.2`, NUL, raw 32-byte host digest,
183	provider-closure digest, harness digest, and SHA256(report bytes), concatenated
184	in that order. Ed25519 keys are provisioned by the authenticated gate outside
185	the report. The gate verifies signature before parsing bounded report bytes.
186	The report's embedded schemaMajor is covered by the signature. Reusing this
187	signature frame for report schema 3 does not make schema 2 bytes schema 3.
188	
189	Authentication proves who supplied the observation; it does not prove the
190	machine executed correctly. The trusted first-party measurement harness,
191	runner observation path and gate are explicit TCB components. The harness must
192	execute the selected closure by verified handle, observe exit/EOF and normalized
193	actual results, and bind the exact measured environment. Product qualification
194	requires retained real measurements from every required lane; synthetic reports
195	are tagged reference-only and cannot be promoted. A producer cannot attest its
196	own unsupported hardware into the allowlist.
197	
198	The original G13 schema/validator remain frozen historical evidence. The new
199	`g13-result-schema.v5.json` and `g13-validator.v5.py` close the reproduced defects
200	for the historical 24-cell shape: independently pinned corpus oracles determine
201	expected atoms and counters, all subject digests join to trusted context, and
202	actual observations plus signature are required. Consistently relabeling every
203	candidate subject digest or zeroing both expected and actual counts now fails.
204	This adapter does not qualify the added JavaScript/Rust cells.
