206	## 3. Full-product matrix and report schema
207	
208	The current native matrix is
209	`native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`. Expand each declared capability/mode
210	cell over its four platform families and each selected signed platform profile
211	from the security contract. A release inventory explicitly selects the
212	advertised supported cells; unsupported typed cells also receive refusal
213	conformance cases. No cell disappears because no runner happened to produce a
214	report. Syntax-only capability is further parameterized by the exact grammar
215	inventory; one grammar's result does not qualify another grammar.
216	
217	The full-product report schema is
218	`foundation/product-quality-report.schema.v3.json`; its gate reference is
219	`foundation/product-quality-validator.py`. A report covers exactly one trusted
220	runner/profile/environment and the required cell set for that lane. CellId is
221	`capability/mode/platform/profile/fixture`; each coordinate comes from the
222	reviewed matrix and corpus expansion, not from report labels. Every required
223	fixture names exact source/input bytes, selected capability/rung, expected
224	normalized observations, expected exit and independently chosen work/stress
225	bounds. Native reference scenarios supply semantic obligations; executable
226	native fixtures and their results must be admitted at implementation
227	qualification before a cell becomes QUALIFIED.
228	
229	The gate's expectedCells is constructed from the verified matrix/corpus and
230	release selection by the first-party gate. It cannot be supplied as a CLI JSON
231	argument, copied out of report fields or recomputed from candidate answers.
232	Expected observation atoms have closed fields `kind`, `subject`, `value` (all
233	strings); `value` is the schema-defined normalized scalar or canonical JSON
234	text for structured payloads. The admitted fixture's normalizer and schema
235	are part of its pinned harness closure. Report atoms sort by canonical bytes,
236	are unique, and must equal the independent oracle exactly. Counts and
237	correctness are calculated by the gate; they are absent from the submitted
238	schema. Duplicate cells/observations, wrong cell sets, wrong exit or substituted
239	answers cannot be hidden by a reported PASS flag because no such flag is read.
240	
241	Each benchmark records 3 warmups followed by 7 measured runs in that order,
242	with positive integer elapsed nanoseconds and peak RSS bytes. The gate calculates median
243	elapsed time and maximum RSS. For an existing baseline the limits are 1.20×
244	median time and 1.25× peak RSS, using checked wide-integer cross multiplication (never wrapping), plus the
245	fixture's independently reviewed absolute bounds. A new supported cell needs
246	an explicitly reviewed initial baseline and absolute budget; absence is not a
247	zero or automatic pass. The two baseline measurements must be both present
248	or both null. A null pair admits an initial-measurement report but never qualifies
249	a release-selected cell; reviewed initial baseline promotion is a separate gate act. Baseline host/provider/harness, fixture, environment and
250	platform profile must be compatible by the release gate's signed inventory;
251	changing the measuring subject cannot silently reuse an unrelated baseline.
252	Cold-start and retained-evidence workloads are separate fixtures, so warmup
253	cannot conceal startup or storage regressions. The old reference adapter
254	retains its historical hardware/performance baseline semantics unchanged.
255	
256	A well-formed authenticated report may report a failing observation. Report
257	admission and release qualification are separate: admission verifies custody,
258	shape and joins; qualification requires every selected cell's correctness and
259	performance to pass on every required profile lane. Missing, unavailable or
260	failed lanes block promotion. The release gate also requires lifecycle,
261	security, output parity and recovery gates; G13 alone never authorizes release.

264	
265	`foundation/check-foundation.py` retains the original integer and G13

292	## 5. Complete product-boundary successor (DR-117)
293	
294	D-371/D-372 prospectively replace P-1/P-2/G3 only as enumerated here. These are the seven dispositions required by architecture file02, “Current V1 product boundary and required successors”; the historical enumeration and preview acceptance keep their original scope.
295	
296	1. **Marketplace/catalog and governance depth:** the selected product has one signed first-party component/recipe/schema registry. It has no public marketplace, third-party publisher admission or ecosystem governance promise. Unknown contributions refuse through the closed registry; declaring an id does not establish trust.
297	2. **External lifecycle parity and discovery:** supported first-party components receive the common installation, update, rollback, offline, doctor and removal contracts. Repository/framework discovery selects applicable admitted capabilities; it is not an external service and cannot install or execute discovered code. Third-party lifecycle parity is outside the selected scope, not a partially specified admission mode.
298	3. **Contribution roles beyond narrow/data-only:** first-party native providers may produce typed facts/Coverage and prepared input imports. Signed first-party declarative recipes/profiles may select host-owned steps. Only the host constructs findings, evaluates policy/verdict, owns persistence, finalization, rendering and termination. A component cannot acquire those powers by declaring a root command or emitting an output record.
299	4. **Untrusted native or WASM admission and enforcement:** neither is admitted in this product. No process/WASM boundary is claimed as a sandbox. Separately authorized repository-code preparation/tests are the explicit trusted-code principal of security S10, with the actual platform disclosure/enforcement matrix and revocation/cleanup rules. They do not open an untrusted plugin admission path. G09/G21/G29/G30 must exercise these refusal and authority boundaries; a synthetic fixture is not enforcement evidence.
300	5. **Imperative contributions, probes, project hooks and root commands:** arbitrary imperative contributions/project hooks/root-parser extensions are not admitted. The closed host command inventory owns every command. Named first-party repair, test, preparation and doctor operations have their exact explicit authorization and effect contracts; a recipe/profile cannot bypass them. Metadata discovery/help/recommend do not run repository hooks or probes. Consent to one executable step never becomes general command or persistence authority.
301	6. **Network-granted analysis and egress defaults:** ordinary analysis/discovery are offline; there is no implicit index refresh, download, telemetry or required egress. Explicit trust refresh/offline import and explicitly required export delivery have their named host lifecycle/output semantics. Repository-code effects are disclosed/admitted by their actual trusted-code grant; they are never silently reclassified as confined analysis. Required delivery failure can fail the invocation without changing a committed Run's assurance.
302	7. **G3 physical substrate:** the selected substrate is a signed Rust distribution core/semantic host, pure first-party evaluator, supervised native TS/JS and Rust components, and the signed offline assets and verified storage mechanics required for the selected authoritative profile. This replaces the prototype's lockstep Node/npm train and the preview's narrow command/provider set. The default product profile is authoritative-capable; an explicitly selected management-only installation is not an authoritative closure and refuses analysis until the required signed closure is separately installed through an authorized lifecycle operation. Missing assets never trigger ambient downloads or a weaker analyzer. Every physical dependency, including compiler/runtime/standard-library/LLVM/storage assets actually used, belongs to the admitted closure/TCB inventory and its packaging/offline/quality gates.
303	
304	The selected exclusions are D-371's credentials, third-party ecosystem, untrusted contributions and TUI exclusions; this section introduces no new scope cut. Product measurements remain required by the named release gates. This is a complete boundary selection now, not a promise that future implementation will choose these policies.

62	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
63	
64	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
65	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
66	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
67	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
68	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
69	`run2`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
70	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
71	that never mint a Run. Schema: `invocation-record.schema.json`.
72	
73	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
74	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
75	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
76	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
77	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
78	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
79	remain separately auditable.
80	
81	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
82	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
83	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
84	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
85	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
86	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
87	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
88	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
89	(crash recovery only).
90	
91	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
92	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
93	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
94	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
95	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
96	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
97	
98	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Generic `mutation` steps use the bare
99	64-hex `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)`. The closed retained
100	scope is exactly `{schemaVersion:1,requestId,stepId,projectId,operation}`, with
101	`operation` equal to `MutationParams.mutationClass`. This explicitly succeeds the
102	former undefined `{operation,projectId,effect preimage}` description. The key is
103	operational and scoped to one host-minted request and admitted immutable step;
104	different fresh requests never deduplicate each other's generic mutations.
105	`sourceStep` resolves inside that same retained invocation, whose admitted
106	parameters and completed dependency results are immutable. Before lookup or
107	replay the host validates the scope and full params, recomputes the key and
108	requires the retained invocation/project/step/operation binding; a caller cannot
109	nominate another invocation's scope or change effect inputs under an old key.
110	Receipt lookup is never an effect-authorization mechanism. A same-scope COMPLETED
111	receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect. Failure, unknown state or
112	incomplete execution requires the operation's existing recovery law, not blind
113	re-execution. Recovery started in a new request retains its own operational scope
114	and the explicit original journal/intent links required by §§6/12.
115	
116	Repair apply is the explicit content-derived exception: it is a dedicated
117	`repair-apply` step, excluded from generic MutationParams. It uses the raw SHA-256 of
118	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
119	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
120	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
121	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
122	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
123	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
124	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
125	
126	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
127	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
128	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
129	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
130	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
131	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
132	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
133	
134	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
135	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
136	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
137	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
138	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
139	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
140	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
141	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
142	
143	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
144	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
145	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
146	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
147	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
148	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
149	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
150	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
151	
152	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
153	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
154	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
155	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
156	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
157	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
158	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
159	
160	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
161	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
162	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
163	No policy file is written implicitly.

167	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
168	
169	`BaselineArtifactV1` lives in the repository as tracked intent
170	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
171	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run2`
172	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
173	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
174	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
175	evaluator, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
176	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
177	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
178	coverage, and sorted unique entries. Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
179	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
180	`closureBundle` reference.
181	
182	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
183	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
184	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
185	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
186	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
187	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
188	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
189	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
190	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
191	executed, whatever bytes are present.
192	
193	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
194	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
195	detector's signed manifest lists the baseline `closure2` as exactly semantically
196	compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`). Otherwise the baseline detector
197	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
198	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
199	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
200	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
201	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
202	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
203	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.

207	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
208	
209	`ComparisonResultV1` (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
210	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
211	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
212	
213	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
214	|---|---|---|---|---|
215	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
216	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
217	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
218	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
219	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
220	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
221	
222	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
223	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
224	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
225	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
226	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
227	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
228	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
229	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
230	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
231	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
232	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
233	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
234	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
235	
236	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
237	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
238	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
239	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
240	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
241	
242	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
243	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
244	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
245	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
246	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
247	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
248	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
249	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
250	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
251	non-gating delta.
252	
253	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
254	
255	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
256	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
257	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
258	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
259	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
260	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
261	
262	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later policy/scope
263	change or by a waiver added in the same change) still gates under
264	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`. Verdict is `fail`
265	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
266	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
267	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
268	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
269	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
270	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

274	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
275	
276	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
277	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
278	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
279	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
280	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
281	
282	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
285	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
286	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
287	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
288	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
289	
290	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
291	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
292	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
293	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
294	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
295	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
296	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
297	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
298	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
299	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
300	
301	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
302	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
303	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
304	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
305	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
306	
307	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
308	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
309	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
310	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
311	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
312	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
313	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
314	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
315	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
316	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
317	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
318	but never feeds a predicate.
319	
320	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
321	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
322	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
323	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
324	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
325	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
326	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.

330	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
331	
332	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV1` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
333	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
334	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
335	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
336	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
337	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
338	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
339	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
340	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
341	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
342	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
343	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
344	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
345	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
346	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
347	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
348	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
349	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
350	The compiled RuleProgramV1 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
351	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
352	
353	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
354	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
355	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
356	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
357	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
358	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
359	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
360	
361	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
362	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
363	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
364	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
365	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
366	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
367	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
368	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
369	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
370	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
371	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
372	
373	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
374	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
375	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
376	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
377	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
378	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
379	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
380	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
381	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
382	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
383	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
384	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
385	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.
386

389	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
390	
391	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
392	
393	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
394	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
395	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
396	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
397	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
398	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
399	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
400	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
401	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
402	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
403	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
404	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
405	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
406	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
407	
408	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
409	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
410	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
411	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
412	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
413	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
414	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
415	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
416	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
417	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
418	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
419	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
420	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
421	
422	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
423	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
424	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
425	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
426	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
427	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
428	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
429	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
430	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
431	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
432	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
433	
434	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
435	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
436	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
437	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
438	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
439	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
440	and remains retained if verification fails.
441

444	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
445	
446	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
447	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
448	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
449	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
450	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
451	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
452	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
453	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
454	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
455	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
456	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
457	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
458	
459	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
460	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
461	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
462	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
463	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
464	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
465	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
466	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
467	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
468	are the supported alternative.

472	## 8. Command inventory, outputs and parity (AR-13 surfaces, AR-16)
473	
474	`workflows/command-inventory.v1.json` is the candidate single inventory,
475	validated by `command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
476	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
477	
478	| Group | Commands |
479	|---|---|
480	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
481	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
482	| mutation | `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `repair apply`, `repair recover`, `purge` |
483	| execution | `test run`, `native prepare` (both explicitly authorized) |
484	| lifecycle / serve / meta | `install`, `update`, `core update|repair|rollback`, trust/store commands, `doctor`, `agent serve`, `help`, `version`, `completion` |
485	
486	Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
487	Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
488	may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
489	its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.
490	
491	**Renderers.** `human` v1, `json` v2 (the `CommandEnvelope` major 2 is the parity
492	reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
493	one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
494	static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
495	disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
496	parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
497	carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
498	`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
499	`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and
500	`retention-disclosure`; inventory admission refuses an omission. SARIF results
501	and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are
502	human/JSON/HTML/agent values; no renderer reads an undeclared findings field or
503	substitutes null for a present verdict/deficiency. Audit adds its comparison
504	fields while preserving the current analysis result. Repair verification adds
505	applied/verified snapshot, snapshot-match, targets-remaining and net-new-findings
506	fields while preserving the fresh verification Run's findings and verdict.
507	An empty findings array is a real empty result; it is never inferred from a
508	missing projection field. Ephemeral analysis retains its existing no-Run rule:
509	`run-id` is explicitly null in the projection's non-authoritative case,
510	never a fabricated Run. Required-output failure still follows the law below.
511	The host projection must be total over the selected command's `parityFields`
512	before a renderer consumes it: every field has its schema-admitted value,
513	including an explicit null only where that field permits it. A missing field
514	or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault, not an empty
515	result or a successful partial rendering: `operational-failed`, exit 4,
516	`faultCause=delivery-required`, `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`. If a Run was already
517	committed, the termination retains its RunId and the after-commit detail below;
518	otherwise no RunId is invented. This classification also covers a pure reference
519	projection helper raising `KeyError`; that exception alone is not a public
520	termination. Actual host exception handling and renderer conformance remain
521	DR-G17/DR-G20 implementation qualification obligations.
522	Requesting a non-applicable format is
523	`REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION` / `OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE` (2). Failure of the selected
524	required renderer **after** a committed Run is `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` (4) with
525	detail `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`, the `runId` in the termination, and
526	no rewrite of the Run; failure of an optional export sink leaves `success`.
527	
528	**Query.** Twenty closed operations over one sealed view (`run2`, `snapshot2` or the
529	`latest` resolver, whose empty domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`), bounded page/items/depth/
530	visited nodes; `completeness=required` at a bound is `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3),
531	best-effort is visible truncation with a cursor. Response context always carries
532	resolved view, Coverage, availability and `advisory` (true exactly for
533	`comparison.diff`, `candidate.list`, `inspection.show`, `review.brief`).
534	
535	**Doctor.** `opensip doctor` produces a typed report over closures, trust, store,
536	platform, project marker and the offline window. A produced report is `success` (0)
537	even when defects are found (detail `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`); CI must inspect
538	`doctor.defectsFound`. Only an unproducible report is `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (4).
539	
540	A `doctor` report is a **different invocation** and therefore cannot deliver the
541	absences of an analysis invocation; `DoctorResult.defects[]` remains the
542	environment report it always was.
543	
544	**Release-availability absence rides the invocation that selected it.**
545	`CommandEnvelope.availability` (`CapabilityAvailabilityV1` =
546	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`, each step
547	`CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1` = `{stepId, noticeCount, notices[]}`) carries
548	every capability the selected product requires (native §1.4) that this release
549	did not declare available, for **every requested unit of every analysis step** —
550	a single-step command projects one step, and a named multi-step invocation
551	projects one entry per analysis step that made a selection. Each notice carries the complete ownership tuple in **typed
552	fields** — `capabilityId`, `languageMode`, `workspaceRoot` — with the existing
553	code `native.capability-unavailable` (a `const`, since the record declares one
554	condition); the tuple is never concatenated into a `subject`, because
555	`workspaceRoot` is a `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024
556	and a truncated path would collapse two distinct units into one indistinguishable
557	notice. The collection is composed **per step** —
558	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`, each step
559	`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}` — because 1024 is the
560	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and *not* an invocation-wide one: two
561	admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices, and no notice is
562	discarded to fit. A step that made no selection contributes no entry, a step that
563	found nothing absent contributes an empty entry, and the same tuple may recur in
564	different steps. Order is the selection's own.
565	
566	Envelope membership alone would **not** deliver it: `render` selects a command's
567	declared `parityFields`, so `capability-availability` is a declared parity field
568	of **every** `requestClass: analysis` command — `default`, `analyze`, `fit`,
569	`audit` and `repair-verify` — and every applicable renderer carries it: human,
570	JSON, SARIF, HTML and agent. Because it is *declared*, it is also **required**:
571	the host projection must be total over the command's parity fields, so a caller
572	whose invocation selected nothing supplies the explicit empty collection
573	(`{stepCount: 0, totalNoticeCount: 0, steps: []}`) rather than omitting the
574	field, and an omission is a required-delivery operational fault under the law
575	above, never a successful partial rendering.
576	
577	It is **advisory** — it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control
578	verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone `Candidate`, since published
579	Candidate records represent actual candidates. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union
580	and is not widened to carry it.
581	
582	**Failure envelopes carry their errors.** A `kind=failure` envelope requires a
583	nonempty `errors` array of `DomainDetail`; where a step termination's optional
584	`domainDetail` is absent, the composition in native §10 supplies the array from
585	the route's own detail code, and where it is present `errors` is exactly that
586	detail so the two surfaces never disagree. Before a Plan or Run exists no run
587	envelope is fabricated.

591	## 9. D9 goldens and typed detail (AR-16)
592	
593	Exit codes are the existing table: success 0, policy-failed 1, request-rejected 2,
594	indeterminate 3, operational-failed 4, interrupted 130. Termination branch contract
595	(schema-enforced): success carries no error/reason/signal; policy-failed carries
596	`runId` or `authority=ephemeral`; request-rejected/operational-failed carry
597	`errorCode` (operational also a non-none `faultCause` from the observation:
598	host-io, ledger-busy, ledger-corrupt, cas-link, provider-protocol, durability-commit,
599	delivery-required, output-serialization, extension-install-io, serve-protocol,
600	host-invariant);
601	indeterminate carries `reasonCodes`; interrupted carries `signal` and a `runId` only
602	when a Run was committed before the interrupt. `DomainDetailCode` is explanatory
603	detail beside an existing code, never a termination code. Selected goldens (the complete retained set
604	is in the inventory and exercised by the model):
605	
606	| Situation | Class / exit | Code | Detail / remedy |
607	|---|---|---|---|
608	| fresh project, providers installed | success 0 | — | DEFAULTED durable retention disclosed; no policy file written |
609	| required provider closure not installed | indeterminate 3 | `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | `COMPONENT.REQUIRED_CLOSURE_NOT_INSTALLED` → `opensip install provider-typescript` |
610	| installed closure bytes corrupt / unspawnable | operational-failed 4 | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` | `DELIVERY.CLOSURE_BYTES_CORRUPT` / `DELIVERY.CLOSURE_UNSPAWNABLE` → `opensip doctor` |
611	| selected renderer fails after commit | operational-failed 4 | `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` | `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`; runId retained |
612	| optional export sink fails | success 0 | — | egress never changes a verdict |
613	| `--ephemeral` with baseline/repair prerequisite | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` | `WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY` |
614	| pivot closure missing / revoked / unmapped project | indeterminate 3 | `BASELINE.RECIPE_UNSUPPORTED` | `BASELINE.PIVOT_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE` / `..._CLOSURE_REVOKED` / `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` |
615	| required evidence lost in audit | indeterminate 3 | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | `COMPARISON.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE` → re-import |
616	| unmapped / corrupt import artifact | request-rejected 2 | `CONFIG.INVALID` | `IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED` / `IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT` |
617	| duplicate waiver / imperative policy key | request-rejected 2 | `CONFIG.INVALID` | `POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER` / `POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED` |
618	| repair preimage mismatch / source moved | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` |
619	| recovery blocked | operational-failed 4 | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` | `REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`; journal retained |
620	| CI interactive test consent / confinement claim | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI` / `TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED` |
621	| doctor report with defects | success 0 | — | `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`; inspect typed outcome |
622	| SIGINT before / after settle | interrupted 130 / settled class | — | after-settle is never reclassified |
623	
624	The exact class/detail pairing is determined by the golden observation and
625	closed schemas. Disclosure-only success details do not imply a clean doctor

89	## 1. Supported native cells (AR-13)
90	
91	### 1.1 Cell coordinates
92	
93	A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
94	matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`, validated by
95	`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`; its `cells` array is the **complete product** of its
96	own `capabilities` and `languageModes`, and the reference checks hold it to
97	exactly that product rather than to a number written here. (A literal count in
98	this prose said `60` while the matrix held 66; a second hand-maintained counter
99	would only go stale again, so the count is derived from the two arrays and
100	reported by the checks instead of restated.) Platform families are exactly the
101	four `platformId`
102	values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
103	`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
104	*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit
105	(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
106	by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.
107	
108	Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
109	qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
110	never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).

112	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
113	
114	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
115	|---|---|---|---|

122	
123	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
124	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
125	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
126	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
127	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
128	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
129	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
130	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
131	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
132	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
133	
134	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
135	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
136	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
137	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
138	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
139	
140	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
141	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
142	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
143	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
144	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
145	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
146	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
147	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
148	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
149	  semantics the mode never computes.
150	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
151	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
152	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
153	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
154	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
155	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
156	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
157	  as a resolution claim.
158	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
159	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
160	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
161	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
162	  suffix must map to one grammar
163	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
164	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
165	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
166	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
167	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
168	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
169	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
170	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
171	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
172	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
173	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
174	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
175	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
176	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
177	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
178	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
179	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
180	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
181	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
182	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
183	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
184	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
185	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
186	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
187	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
188	
189	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
190	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
191	
192	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
193	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
194	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
195	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
196	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
197	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
198	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
199	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
200	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
201	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
202	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
203	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
204	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
205	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
206	
207	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
208	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
209	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
210	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
211	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
212	languages instead of ignoring four.
213	
214	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
215	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
216	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
217	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
218	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
219	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
220	
221	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
222	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
223	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
224	
225	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
226	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
227	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
228	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
229	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
230	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
231	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
232	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
233	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
234	whether facts happen to exist:
235	
236	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
237	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
238	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
239	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
240	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
241	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
242	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
243	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
244	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
245	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
246	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
247	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
248	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
249	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
250	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
251	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
252	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
253	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
254	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
255	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
256	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
257	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
258	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
259	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
260	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
261	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
262	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
263	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
264	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
265	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
266	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
267	  exactly as the matrix already says.
268	
269	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
270	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
271	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
272	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
273	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
274	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
275	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
276	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
277	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
278	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
279	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
280	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
281	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
282	
283	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
284	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
285	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
286	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
287	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
288	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
289	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
290	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
291	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
292	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
293	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
294	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
295	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
296	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
297	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
298	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
299	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
300	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
301	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
302	cross-universe defect.
303	
304	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
305	**not** contain is owed nothing —
306	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
307	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
308	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
309	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
310	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
311	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
312	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
313	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
314	row, and never inferred.
315	
316	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
317	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
318	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
319	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
320	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
321	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
322	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
323	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
324	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
325	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
326	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
327	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
328	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
329	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
330	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
331	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
332	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
333	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
334	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
335	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
336	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
337	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
338	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
339	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
340	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
341	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
342	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
343	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
344	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
345	
346	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
347	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
348	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
349	
350	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
351	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
352	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
353	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
354	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
355	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
356	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
357	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
358	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
359	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
360	
361	The guard is **syntax-universe specific**. Every capability of the TypeScript and
362	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
363	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
364	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
365	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
366	compiler-ownership obligation.
367	
368	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
369	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
370	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
371	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
372	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
373	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
374	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
375	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
376	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
377	supported one.
378	
379	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
380	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
381	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
382	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
383	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating
384	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
385	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
386	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
387	scope therefore remains admissible.
388	
389	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
390	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
391	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
392	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
393	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
394	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
395	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
396	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
397	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
398	
399	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
400	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
401	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
402	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
403	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
404	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
405	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
406	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
407	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.
408	
409	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
410	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
411	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
412	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

439	- **L-JS1** synthesized options: `paths`/`baseUrl`/`rootDirs`/custom `types` are unknown; a specifier resolvable only through them is `unresolved-module-specifier`.

Declarative `macro_rules!` expansion is compiler-native and fully supported.

449	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
450	
451	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
452	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
453	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
454	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
455	share a root.
456	
457	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
458	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
459	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
460	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
461	
462	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
463	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
464	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
465	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.

467	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
468	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
469	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is

471	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
472	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
473	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`

476	  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package

478	  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
479	  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
