746	  native.capability-unavailable`, not the whole `DomainDetailCode` enum: this
747	  typed record declares exactly one condition, and an earlier revision admitted
748	  `CONFIG.INVALID` on a release-absence notice.
749	- **Declared parity, not merely envelope membership.** Being present on the
750	  envelope does not make a field part of renderer parity — `render` selects only
751	  a command's declared `parityFields`, so the collection reached JSON and agent
752	  and was omitted by human, SARIF and HTML. `capability-availability` is now a
753	  declared parity field of every `requestClass: analysis` command (`default`,
754	  `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `repair-verify`), so every applicable renderer
755	  carries it.
756	- **Authority limits.** The disclosure is **advisory**: it terminates nothing,
757	  mints no Coverage, creates no Control verdict and no repair authority, and
758	  fabricates no clone `Candidate` — the published Candidate records represent
759	  actual candidates, so an absent provider can never be one. Nothing here
760	  truncates: a step's `notices` is bounded by the analysis-spec request bound it
761	  can never exceed, and `steps` by the invocation's own step bound, so
762	  `noticeCount` and `totalNoticeCount` are exact rather than a residue of a
763	  dropped tail.
764	- **Which capabilities use which route.** A **fact-producing** capability keeps
765	  its `relation@rung` Coverage under the existing precedence, and this detail
766	  does not replace it. A **candidate-only** capability has no Coverage entry at
767	  all, so this detail is its *only* public route. No new vocabulary, no new
768	  public code, **no preview or default exception**.
769	- **What an absence projects to, and what wins when two apply.** Neither case may
770	  be assumed. *Precedence*: a capability can be undeclared **and** unservable by
771	  the admitted universe at once — `references` under `syntax-only` is both. The
772	  syntax capability prerequisite *derives* `language-tier-unsupported` /
773	  `capability-missing` for such a scope and refuses anything else, and §10's
774	  precedence ranks `language-tier-unsupported` ahead of `provider-unavailable`,
775	  so the more specific one wins and the release-absence account never overrides
776	  it. Where no more specific deficiency applies, `provider-unavailable` with
777	  `capability-missing` is the applicable pair on the existing
778	  `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` route. *Candidate-only capabilities*:
779	  `clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs` have **empty** matrix `relations` — they
780	  are candidate-only by §6.1 authority, mint no fact and no `relation@rung`, and
781	  therefore have **no Coverage entry** that could carry a pair; requiring one
782	  would mean fabricating a relation. Their account is the selection record itself
783	  (`projection: selection-account-only`), while fact-producing capabilities carry
784	  `projection: coverage-entry` and name the exact `relation@rung` coordinates
785	  they project onto. An availability account may be shared by all capabilities;
786	  it is automatically a Coverage result for none of them.
787	- **Availability is not qualification.** Declaring a capability cannot promote a
788	  cell: `platformQualified` stays false, no cell is `QUALIFIED`, and
789	  `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` remains "contracted behavior, corpus named, qualification
790	  pending" whatever a release declares. A staged or development build shipping
791	  fewer providers is an availability fact disclosed per request — not a narrowed
792	  product and not a completed release qualification.
793	- **Explicit configuration overrides the request, not the obligation.**
794	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities` uses this same vocabulary; an
795	  override is a recorded choice with its own provenance (the default's is
796	  `DEFAULTED`). A user narrowing their own analysis is visible; a host silently
797	  narrowing the product would not be.
798	- **The host input boundary, honestly.** *Which* rows a release ships is an
799	  authenticated input this contract cannot measure, and nothing here qualifies a
800	  build, an installer or a provider. What is contract is the obligation the
801	  default must meet, the membership the declaration is held to, and the
802	  disclosure an absence owes.
803	- **Closed at admission, not only in the helper.** The default helper is one
804	  producer of an `analysis-spec`, not the authority. The same vocabulary is
805	  closed again at Plan/Run closure over the **retained** `analysis-spec`
806	  (`ANALYSIS_SPEC_CAPABILITY:native.requested-capability-*`), so an explicitly
807	  configured or hand-built spec is judged by exactly the rule a defaulted one is,
808	  and the default and explicit paths agree on one spelling by construction. The
809	  foundation keeps its own fault for an unregistered *mode*; native owns which
810	  capabilities exist and which cells this product promises anything for.
811	
812	No capability is added, removed or renamed, no cell state changes, and all six
813	advertised modes, the three native contexts and the full default-selected
814	product stay exactly as representable as before. What is new is the authority
815	for a field that had none.
816	
817	**Backup custody join.** Dependency-source files, inert prepared rows and
818	generated-file blobs are host CAS objects under the one host storage root; they
819	inherit the identity-and-evidence §5 backup-managed-storage choice
820	(`--allow-backup-custody` or an admitted storage-policy record; CI without a
821	choice refuses `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `storage.backup-choice-required`).
822	Native adds no second store and no custody rule of its own.
823	
824	`mixed-native-partial` fixes the meaning: TypeScript unit complete, co-located Rust
825	unit missing an external crate → TypeScript-scoped predicates evaluate;
826	repository-scoped semantic predicates are indeterminate with
827	`input-closure-incomplete` naming the crate; syntax and clone predicates complete
828	for both.

832	## 2. Semantic universe successors
833	
834	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
835	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
836	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
837	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
838	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
839	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
840	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
841	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
842	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
843	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
844	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.

870	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
871	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
872	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
873	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
874	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
875	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
876	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
877	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
878	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
879	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
880	never an ADMIT. It refuses when

882	- the admission is not a Rust context admission, or the universe names a context
883	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;
884	- any overlapping field disagrees:

892	  dependency set, toolchain, cfg set or preparation kind;

895	  bytes in custody never enter a resolution by being in custody;
896	- the snapshot does not contain what the universe names: `Cargo.lock` missing or

989	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
990	
991	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
992	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
993	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
994	own language and refuses the other.
995	
996	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
997	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
998	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
999	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
1000	
1001	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
1002	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
1003	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
1004	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
1005	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
1006	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure

1008	
1009	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
1010	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
1011	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
1012	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
1013	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
1014	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a

1016	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
1017	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.

1019	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
1020	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
1021	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).

1027	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,

1031	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],

1037	
1038	| Field | Produced from |
1039	|---|---|
1040	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
1041	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
1042	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |

1044	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` names the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must be covered by a retained component |
1045	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1046	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1047	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
1048	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
1049	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |

1051	
1052	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1053	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1054	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1055	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1056	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1057	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1058	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1059	
1060	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1061	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1062	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1063	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1064	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1065	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1066	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1067	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1068	
1069	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1070	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1071	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1072	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1073	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1074	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1075	
1076	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1077	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1078	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1079	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1080	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1081	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1082	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1083	the admitted id refuse
1084	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1085	
1086	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1087	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1088	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1089	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1090	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1091	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1092	
1093	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1094	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1095	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no case-insensitive duplicate names,
1096	and selects the same case-insensitive name set as the honored `lib` list;
1097	each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context

1140	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1141	
1142	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1143	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1144	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1145	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1146	
1147	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1148	
1149	| Field | Rule |
1150	|---|---|
1151	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1152	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1153	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1154	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1155	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1156	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1157	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1158	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1159	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1160	
1161	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1162	
1163	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1164	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1165	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1166	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1167	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1168	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1169	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1170	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1171	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1172	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1173	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1174	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1175	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1176	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1177	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1178	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1179	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1180	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1181	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1182	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1183	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1184	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1185	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1186	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1187	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1188	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1189	  syntax analysis.
1190	
1191	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1192	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1193	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1194	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

1210	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;

1212	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),

1217	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1218	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):

1298	`{schemaVersion:3, preparation: {kind: authorized-execution|imported-descriptor,
1299	authorizationId|null, importId|null, toolchain, dependencySourceSetId, cfgSetId,

1301	
1302	`PreparedOutputRowV3`: `{kind, ownerKey, configuration, site|null, generated|null,

1308	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:

1310	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),
1311	  `macro-expansion` (`text/x-rust-expansion`: the fully expanded token text for one
1312	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
1313	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
1314	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file

1316	  `build-script-binary` are refused **regardless of the media type they claim**

1322	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
1323	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
1324	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).

1326	  The worker resolves `env!("OUT_DIR")` for owner *O* to the read-only virtual
1327	  path `.opensip/out/v1/<ownerKey>/` in its sealed VFS. A site
1328	  `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"))` (likewise
1329	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to
1330	  `(ownerKey, logicalPath="generated.rs")` whose `inputBinding` equals the current

1341	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
1342	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to

1368	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1369	
1370	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1371	
1372	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1373	
1374	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1375	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1376	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1377	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1378	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1379	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1380	
1381	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1382	
1383	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1384	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1385	
1386	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1387	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1388	
1389	```
1390	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1391	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1392	```
1393	
1394	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1395	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1396	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1397	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1398	
1399	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1400	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1401	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1402	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1403	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1404	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1405	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1406	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1407	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1408	
1409	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1410	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1411	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1412	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1413	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1414	against a value the provider never supplied.
1415	
1416	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1417	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1418	
1419	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1420	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1421	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1422	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1423	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1424	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1425	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1426	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1427	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1428	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1429	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1430	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1431	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1432	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1433	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1434	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1435	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1436	
1437	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1438	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1439	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1440	
1441	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1442	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1443	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1444	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1445	
1446	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1447	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1448	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1449	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1450	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1451	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1452	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
1453

1582	
1583	`ClosedWorldV2` = `{exportsClosed: closed|open|unknown, entryPointsRecognized:
1584	all|partial|none, nonliteralLoading: none|present, externalConsumers:
1585	none-declared|possible|unknown, dynamicDispatch: resolved|present|not-applicable,

1595	   `reflective-access`, `indirect-eval` edges in the universe);
1596	4. `externalConsumers=none-declared` (the user/policy declares no non-repository
1597	   consumers: no published subpath, no sibling deployment reading the tree).

1599	`private:true` alone is `unknown` (`private-true-alone-is-not-closed`). A
1600	universal-negative predicate on an exported subject of an `open`/`unknown`
1601	universe with `externalConsumerPolicy=forbid` reports `external-consumers-unknown`.

1603	**Dynamic edges propagate.** `affected_targets` marks every subject a dynamic
1604	edge could reach: `targetScope=module` marks all exports of `targetModule`;
1605	`universe` marks all subjects of the universe; `external`/`unknown` marks every

1617	### 4.6 Sufficiency v2 (replaces `$.sufficiency`)
1618	
1619	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
1620	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.
1621	
1622	1. Relation absent from the view → `required-relation-missing`.
1623	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.
1624	3. `confidenceMillionths < minConfidenceMillionths` → `confidence-floor-unmet`.
1625	4. Relation `types` with `derivationPolicy=declared-only` and any `compiler-inferred` derivation in the view → `derivation-policy-unmet`.
1626	5. `completeness=complete` and `coverage≠complete` → the entry's own deficiency.
1627	6. `quantifier=universal-negative`: state `partial` or `not-attempted` → `resolution-incomplete` regardless of policy; state `incomplete` or target affected by a dynamic edge → `forbid`: `resolution-incomplete`; `disclose`: disclosure `{unresolved-edges, count, classes}`.
1628	7. `quantifier=universal-negative`, target exported and `exportsClosed≠closed` → `forbid`: `external-consumers-unknown`; `assume-closed`: disclosure.
1629	8. Dependencies (`dependsOn`) recursively (depth ≤ 4) with `partial-ok` for existential requirements and the parent's quantifier/policies for universal negatives.
1630	
1631	There is no early exit. A one-rung relation under `existential` with
1632	`partial-ok` passes step 5 vacuously but still runs steps 1–4 and 8: the former
1633	step 9 shortcut ("satisfied outright") returned before the confidence floor and
1634	let confidence 100000 pass a floor of 900000; it was removed (post-reset
1635	SHOULD-4) and the regression case
1636	`sufficiency-v2-confidence-floor-precedes-one-rung-existential-shortcut`
1637	checks that v2 and the retained v1 oracle both yield `confidence-floor-unmet`
1638	for `clones` at 100000 under floor 900000, and `satisfied` at 1000000.

1640	### 4.7 Positive coverage case (`positive-static-consumer`)
1641	
1642	Module A exports `foo` and `bar`; module B does `import {foo} from './a'; foo();`
1643	No computed access, no dynamic import, `package.json private:true` without
1644	published entries, explicit entry points, no external consumers declared.
1645	Provider emits `references@resolved-binding` for `foo`, zero `unresolved-edge`
1646	facts, the stage completes, `resolutionCompleteness.complete`,
1647	`exportsClosed=closed`. Then "no consumer of `foo`" → satisfied=false by evidence;
1648	"no consumer of `bar`" under `universal-negative/forbid/forbid` → satisfied=true
1649	with no deficiency. That is the only shape under which an authoritative
1650	no-consumer claim is eligible. No provider verdict exists.

1652	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
1653	
1654	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
1655	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
1656	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
1657	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
1658	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
1659	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
1660	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
1661	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
1662	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
1663	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
1664	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
1665	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.

1669	## 5. Native execution boundary (AR-07)
1670	
1671	### 5.1 Principal class `repository-code` and its joins (R4)
1672	
1673	The security contract S10 registers principal class `repository-code`
1674	(`RepoExecutionGrantV2`, execution classes `build-script | proc-macro |
1675	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and
1676	checked by schema constants:
1677	
1678	| Where | Spelling | Role |
1679	|---|---|---|
1680	| security S10 / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.principalClass` | `repository-code` | principal class of the admitted grant |
1681	| foundation `identity-schemas.v2#semantic-grant.principals[].kind` / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.semanticGrantPrincipalKind` | `trusted-repository-code` | Plan-bound semantic projection `{kind, closureId (tool closure), ownerSourceDigest (owner file manifest)}` with `analysisOperations ∋ prepare-code` |
1682	| workflow test-execution / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.workflowPrincipalSpelling` | `P-TRUSTED-REPO` | the workflow step's constant for the same principal (class `test-runner`) |
1683	
1684	The **authority grant** is the operational `authorizationRef`
1685	(`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)`, the workflow's `securityGrantRef`):
1686	it is excluded from the Plan descriptor and from every content identity
1687	(`authorized-execution-interactive-with-declared-owner-disclosed` checks
1688	`authorizationRefInPlan=false`). The **semantic grant projection** is what the Plan
1689	binds. A universe with `preparedResolution=imported-inert` projects only
1690	`read-import`; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code`. Prepared semantic
1691	availability therefore never implies that this host holds or held an execution
1692	grant (`prepared-imported-inert-implies-no-host-execution-grant`).
1693	
1694	The principal, identified by `{projectId, snapshotId, ownerKey,
1695	ownerFileManifestSha256, toolchainDigest}`, is **outside** the first-party TCB.
1696	Executing it in-host is a disclosed trusted-code execution of code the user chose
1697	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a
1698	platform primitive is enforced. The security owner supplies the revocation clock
1699	and cancellation carrier (H-2).
1700	
1701	### 5.2 `AuthorizedExecutionV2`
1702	
1703	Domain `native.authorized-execution.v2`. Closed descriptor bound into
1704	`rust-v2.executionCapableResolution` via `preparedOutputSetId`: `{schemaVersion:2,
1705	operation:"native.prepare", principalClass:"repository-code", projectId,
1706	snapshotId (snapshot2), dependencySourceSetId, toolchain, toolClosure, cfgSetId,
1707	owners: [{ownerKey, kind: build-script|proc-macro, ownerFileManifestSha256,
1708	provenanceAssurance: registry-authenticated|declared|in-snapshot}], effects:
1709	{subprocess, filesystemWrite, network, environment: {requested, enforcement}},
1710	authorization: {mode: interactive-explicit|policy-record, policyRecordId|null, ci},
1711	liveBoundaries: {revocationCheck: before-each-owner, cancellation:
1712	process-group-kill, trustClockRequired: true}, bounds}`.
1713	
1714	`EnforcementV1` values are **copied from the security owner's platform truth
1715	table**; this contract never asserts an `ENFORCED-PLATFORM` value itself, and the
1716	model refuses a record that claims more than the pinned table (`permission-truth-tables.v9.json`:
1717	`network`/`subprocess`/`filesystemWrite` `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`; `environment`
1718	`ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION`).
1719	
1720	**Which token each effect name is copied from (CB4-ADV-3).** The four effect
1721	names here are `effects` field names; the pinned table is over seven closed
1722	permission **tokens**, and the correspondence was determinate by elimination but
1723	published nowhere, so an implementer had to infer it. It is stated:
1724	
1725	| `effects` field | Permission token | `ENFORCED` in v9 (child-process) | What the value means |
1726	|---|---|---|---|
1727	| `subprocess` | `PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | No mechanism prevents the effect; the record states what was asked and answered. |
1728	| `filesystemWrite` | `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. See the scope note below. |
1729	| `network` | `PT-NET-EGRESS` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. |
1730	| `environment` | `PT-ENV-READ` | `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` | The child's environment is constructed by the host, so the capability is never conferred *in this execution mode*. |
1731	
1732	Three scope facts travel with that table and none of them may be dropped:
1733	
1734	1. **The values are per execution mode.** `native.prepare` runs owners as child
1735	   processes, so the `child-process` column is the applicable one. In v9's
1736	   `in-host-process` mode *every* token including `PT-ENV-READ` is
1737	   `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, because a component sharing the host's address space shares
1738	   its environment. Quoting `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` without its mode would
1739	   over-claim.
1740	2. **`PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` is not repository filesystem authority.** The token
1741	   names the *host's own state store*. Neither it nor any grant over it confers
1742	   authority over the repository tree, and its `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` value says
1743	   precisely that nothing prevents writes anywhere: the executing code holds the
1744	   invoking user's ambient authority throughout. `filesystemWrite` here is a
1745	   disclosure of that fact, never a scoping of it.
1746	3. **`PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED` is deliberately unprojected.** It is the one token
1747	   whose v9 value is `ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER`, and no `effects` field carries
1748	   it, because repository code under `native.prepare` is not routed through a
1749	   host broker. `EnforcementV1` admits the value, so the vocabulary is not
1750	   narrowed; nothing in this contract claims it. The two read-only tokens
1751	   (`PT-FS-READ-PROJECT`, `PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT`) are likewise unprojected: they
1752	   are not effects this record authorizes.
1753	
1754	Confinement is never claimed, and every value above remains the security owner's
1755	to change: if a primitive is later measured on a platform, only that cell moves.
1756	
1757	The mandatory pre-execution sentence, in human and
1758	JSON output: "Build scripts and procedural macros from N packages will run with
1759	your user's authority. OpenSIP does not prevent network access or other effects on
1760	this platform." followed, when applicable, by "Packages with declared
1761	(unauthenticated) provenance: …".
1762	
1763	Authorization: interactive → explicit per-invocation confirmation naming the
1764	owners; CI (`ci=true`) → never prompts; requires a pre-existing `policy-record`
1765	bound to the same `dependencySourceSetId` and toolchain, else
1766	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `native.execution-not-authorized`. Missing live
1767	boundaries, an unavailable bundled linker, or an over-claimed enforcement value
1768	refuse the same way. Authorization is never inherited by another ProjectId,
1769	snapshot with a different owner manifest, or toolchain.

1771	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
1772	
1773	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
1774	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
1775	
1776	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
1777	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
1778	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
1779	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
1780	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
1781	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
1782	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
1783	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
1784	   nothing is installed).
1785	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
1786	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
1787	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
1788	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
1789	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
1790	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
1791	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
1792	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
1793	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
1794	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
1795	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
1796	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
1797	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
1798	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
1799	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
1800	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
1801	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
1802	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
1803	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
1804	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
1805	
1806	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
1807	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
1808	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
1809	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
1810	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
1811	supply a dylib.

1813	### 5.4 Failure, retry, cancellation, recovery
1814	
1815	| Event | Outcome |
1816	|---|---|
1817	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |
1818	| Revocation observed before an owner | step stops; no further owner runs; rows already captured are discarded; `request-rejected` (`native.execution-not-authorized`) |
1819	| Wall or byte bound exceeded | whole step `operational-failed` (4); no row admitted. Existing `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with detail `native.prepare-bound-exceeded`. Not `BudgetExhausted`: a preparation bound is a safety bound of the adapter |
1820	| Cancellation | kill the process group, discard partial OUT_DIR and captured rows, `interrupted` (130) |
1821	| Retry | idempotent by `(dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId, owners manifest)`; an identical inert set already in custody is reused without re-execution and without re-prompt when a policy record covers it |
1822	| Host crash mid-step | scratch reclaimed by ordinary crash reconciliation; no partial set is visible to Plan construction |
1823	| Ambient Cargo config found | `operational-failed` (4), `native.ambient-cargo-config`; never merged |
1824	| Imported set replaces in-host preparation | allowed; PO-0/PO-1/PO-3 apply |
1825

1827	
1828	No sandbox is claimed. No DR-128 scope opens. No general test runner is defined
1829	here (AR-08, workflow owner). The TypeScript side selects no repository execution
1830	(`executionCapableResolution=false`); `postinstall` scripts, bundler plugins and
1831	`ts-node` transforms are never run. "No network fetch" is a design invariant of
1832	first-party code, not an enforced bound on repository code.

1856	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
1857	
1858	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
1859	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
1860	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
1861	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
1862	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
1863	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
1864	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
1865	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
1866	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
1867	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
1868	
1869	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
1870	|---|---|---|---|
1871	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
1872	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
1873	
1874	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
1875	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
1876	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.

1879	
1880	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
1881	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
1882	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
1883	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
1884	
1885	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
1886	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
1887	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
1888	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.

1890	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),

1892	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason

1894	- Output rows carry `projectionId=tsjs-erasure-v1`, `authority=candidate-only`,
1895	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
1896	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,
1897	  never a repair prerequisite.

1899	Cases: `clone-cross-tsjs-candidate-only`, `clone-cross-tsjs-runtime-significant-excluded`.

2386	**A refused value can exceed the diagnostic bound, and the projection is
2387	bounded.** `DomainDetail.subject` is `BoundedText` (1024) while a *structurally
2388	valid* `languageMode` may be 4096 characters; the composed subject then reached
2389	4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at
2390	`termination.domainDetail.subject` or `errors[0].subject`. `bounded_subject`
2391	elides: the registered **key** is preserved verbatim — it selects the code, the
2392	class and the origin — and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading
2393	window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. Emitting the untruncated
2394	string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and
2395	reclassifying the input error as success would be false. The code, class and
2396	origin are never changed by the elision.

2398	The encoding is normative, and its **units** are stated because they differ
2399	between the two operations. Let `raw` be the composed subject
2400	`<registered key>[:<value>]` as an **admitted Unicode scalar string**. Length and
2401	slicing count **Unicode code points**, which is what `BoundedText`'s JSON Schema
2402	`maxLength` counts — not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units. If
2403	`len(raw) ≤ 1024` the subject **is** `raw`. Otherwise it is
2404	
2405	```
2406	raw[: 1024 − len("...#sha256:") − 64] + "...#sha256:" + hex(SHA256(raw.encode("utf-8")))
2407	```
2408	
2409	— the marker `...#sha256:` is ASCII, the digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex
2410	characters, the SHA-256 input is exactly `raw` encoded as UTF-8 with **no**
2411	additional normalization, and the result is exactly 1024 code points. A
2412	non-ASCII value therefore has a UTF-8 byte length that may exceed 1024 while its
2413	scalar length does not, and the two operations must not be conflated.
2414	
2415	Two distinct long values are distinguished under the **ordinary
2416	collision-resistance assumption** for SHA-256; this is not a claim that collision
2417	is impossible. **The guarantee is confined to what is published** — the bounded
2418	subject and its digest. This contract does **not** promise a separate retained
2419	store of the untruncated value and names none; a host that keeps its own
2420	operational log may match it by recomputing this digest, which is why the digest
2421	is published at all.

2504	ownership disclosure.
2505	
2506	A **deliberately excluded** selection is not an unfinished enumeration and owes
2507	no disclosure. The owner exists, enumeration is complete, and the path is
2508	compiled only by targets outside the selection: the host examined that subject
2509	and correctly produced no fact, so `complete` remains lawful. A selection is
2510	committed in the universe identity and visible to every consumer; unfinished
2511	enumeration leaves no such trace. Collapsing the two would either hide a real
2512	gap or slander a lawful selection. The remaining
2513	selection-law refusals get no cause and that is deliberate:
2514	`BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED` and `BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED` are
2515	per-body refusals §11 states are compatible with `coverage: complete`, and
2516	`BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT`/`BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS` refuse at the
2517	universe before any Coverage entry exists. The body refusal itself is unchanged:
2518	a producer that cannot mint a body identity still must not pretend to, and an
2519	empty clones Coverage remains indeterminate rather than a finding of no clones.
2520	
2521	**Fault law (R7; `stage_authority`, `run_termination`, `StageAuthorityV1`).**
2522	A worker that faults — process fault, protocol violation, `ProviderFault` frame,
2523	crash — contributes **no facts, no Coverage entries and no Run**: its diagnostics
2524	(stderr, fault detail) are an operational record only and can never mint an
2525	authoritative fact; the invocation is `operational-failed` (4)
2526	`PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`; cancellation is `interrupted` (130) with the same
2527	no-facts rule (`fault-worker-diagnostics-never-mint-facts-or-run`). By contrast a
2528	stage that terminates cleanly over **successfully admitted but incomplete inputs**
2529	(missing crate, generated file unavailable, unresolved edges) yields admitted
2530	facts and typed Coverage, seals an **authoritative** Run, and terminates
2531	`indeterminate` (3) with the deficiency as typed detail in the coverage2 record
2532	(`admitted-incomplete-inputs-yield-authoritative-indeterminate-3`).
2533	`BudgetExhausted` and `Unavailable` are clean typed terminals: facts before the
2534	terminal are admitted and the Run is authoritative with the stage `partial`.

2676	
2677	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
2678	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
2679	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
2680	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
2681	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
2682	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
2683	make it so.
2684	
2685	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
2686	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
2687	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
2688	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
2689	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
2690	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
2691	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
2692	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
2693	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
2694	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
2695	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
2696	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
2697	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
2698	
2699	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
2700	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
2701	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
2702	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
2703	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
2704	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
2705	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
2706	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
2707	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
2708	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
2709	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
2710	
2711	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
2712	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
2713	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
2714	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
2715	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.
2716	This record states what a producer claims it enumerated; it admits no compiler,
2717	measures no build and qualifies no enumerator.

2899	Public details for the shared cap and explicit-root grammar are PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT and PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID. The pure instrument retains native.too-many-units and native.explicit-root-grammar only as internal aliases; the host normalizes them through public-detail-registry.v1.json, and the public schema rejects those aliases. The internal capability table key provider-unavailable/capability-missing emits native.capability-unavailable publicly.
2900	
2901	The four repository-code child-process effect selections in §5 are consistent with the accepted permission-truth-tables.v9 head. The v7→v9 changes concern metadata/recording and the host-under-instruction network recital; the permission table rows supplying the four selections are unchanged. The product still declares these as its own supported-platform design selections, not measured confinement or an extension of preview qualification.
2902	
2903	
2904	A **bounded selection array** that exceeds its published schema bound refuses REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE (request-rejected, exit2), public detail PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT and subject `field:count>limit`; it is never truncated. **Four** fields are bounded this way, across **two record families**, and the subject always names which one overflowed. The **scope descriptor** family contributes three: workspaceRoots has limit1024 (distinct roots after co-located unit deduplication), and pathPrefixes/excludedPathPrefixes each65536; thus1025..4096 valid discovered unit roots produce this typed scope refusal, while more than4096 first-party unit directories produce PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT earlier. The **analysis-spec** array `requestedCapabilities` has limit1024, and it overflows for a reason worth stating: the matrix-fixed default requests one row per (discovered unit, capability whose cell is not NOT-SELECTED), which is11 capabilities per TypeScript unit and10 per Rust unit, so93 TypeScript units fit, at1023 rows - one row under the bound, not exactly at it - and94 do not, at1034. Units94..1024 are therefore ordinary repositories the scope law admits and the default analysis cannot express, and they refuse HERE rather than through a generic schema exception that names no field, count or limit. The public code is shared across host/native scope admission; callers must narrow explicit selection — for `requestedCapabilities` that means fewer workspace roots for the invocation, or an explicit `analysis.capabilities` selection carrying its own provenance. Native ScopeRefusal retains detail, D9 and observed bound fields for the host's closed termination projection, and is already field-generic, so all four fields use one law and one code: the remedy class is identical — narrow the selection explicitly, nothing was truncated — which is why widening it across the second record family adds no public code.
2905	
2906	The **pre-Plan admission order** is published, because it is what makes the typed refusal reachable. A complete `analysis-spec` - defaulted or explicitly supplied - is admitted in three steps: **bounded selection cardinality first**, then generic schema validation of the whole record, then the closed native capability vocabulary. Cardinality precedes schema validation because a `maxItems` breach is reported generically, restating the entire instance and naming no field, count or limit; an oversized ordinary selection is not a malformed record and is not published as one. The first step is **conditional on the field actually being a JSON array in an object**, and nothing is coerced: a missing field, a null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is. Without that condition a 1025-character string would be published as 1025 capabilities, which is a misclassification and not a scope limit. Everything a schema is genuinely better at - an unknown property, a wrong type, a missing field, a missing `schemaVersion` - still refuses at the schema step exactly as before. One condition is reordered for one shape, and none is added. This order is the **request** boundary only. Validation of a **retained** `analysis-spec` payload at Run closure is a different question with a different answer - an oversized array there means corruption rather than an oversized request - and nothing here changes it: Run closure schema-validates the retained record before any capability vocabulary admission, so an over-long retained array already refuses there.
2907	
2908	What this refusal is **not**. It is not a truncation: no capability is dropped, no root is dropped, and the matrix-fixed default and every advertised capability promise are unchanged. It is not a host defect: the host computed the default correctly and the *request* simply cannot be expressed within a published bound, so it is `request-rejected`/`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` and never `host-invariant`. It is not a licence to shard the invocation, execute extra steps or raise a bound — any of those would be a new product capability and none is selected here. And it is **pre-Plan for the analysis step it refuses**: that step mints no `plan2` and no `run2`. That is a statement about the step, not about attribution - the request and the invocation keep their ordinary operational attribution under the workflow law, and any earlier step of the same invocation that already committed an outcome keeps it. A pure helper `ValidationError` is not a public termination, which is exactly why the typed refusal exists.
2909	
2910	The standalone boundary-crossing key native.explicit-root-crosses-boundary is an internal alias of PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID, the code security emits before native on the operational path. native.boundary-inventory-mismatch is an internal alias of PROJECT.DISCOVERY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH. The latter public condition is emitted by the actual host when its native marker/file inventory disagrees with the security discovery inventory (REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, exit2), including before native is invoked. Neither internal spelling is a public enum value.

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
130	
131	An explicit source suppresses automatic discovery. Every directory from the
132	root to a unit must pass directory custody and stay inside the root (no
133	absolute, `.`, `..`, backslash or NUL segments); every marker file must pass
134	file custody. A manifest is **data**: discovery records its presence and later
135	readers parse it as data only, never running scripts, hooks, plugins or
136	workspace globs and never writing source.

177	Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful

184	**Pruned trees and the read set (A-5).** "No custody walk" for a pruned tree

242	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
243	
244	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
245	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
246	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
247	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
248	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
249	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.
250	
251	Decision evaluation, in order, for record R, observation (wall W, sleep-
252	inclusive monotonic M, bootId B), optional payload P:
253	
254	1. Payload future check (unchanged FC-FUTURE): an issue time > W + 24 h refuses
255	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`; nothing is written.
256	2. Fresh install (F absent): without admitted time evidence the evaluation
257	   refuses `TRUST.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (the core's embedded bootstrap
258	   payload or an ordinary payload is required); nothing is written. With it,
259	   W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` and initialises nothing.
260	   Otherwise tEval = max(W, A); F := tEval, L := A, anchor := (B, M, W); expiry
261	   states are evaluated from the presented documents, never set to false.
262	3. In-session continuity: if the anchor has the same bootId, expected =
263	   anchorWall + (M − anchorMono). A forward deviation over 24 h refuses
264	   `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` (`in-session`) unless a witness proves the
265	   expectation itself was behind (witness ≥ expected). A backward deviation is
266	   the finding `CLOCK-REGRESSION-IN-SESSION`; a monotonic value below the
267	   anchor's is `CLOCK-CONTINUITY-MALFORMED` (finding, anchor not rewritten).
268	4. Plausibility: W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD`
269	   (`beyond-horizon`) **before any evaluation and before any write**. Remedy:
270	   correct the clock, or present a payload issued within 90 d of W.
271	5. Evaluation: tEval = max(F, W, A). The floor written is exactly tEval
272	   (write-ahead, §5.6 durability), so the persisted floor and the evaluated
273	   instant never differ and no later evaluation runs earlier than an earlier
274	   one. `CLOCK-REGRESSION` (W < F) and `TRUST.FLOOR_AHEAD_OF_WALL`
275	   (F > W + 90 d) are findings with remedies. L advances to A when A > L. The
276	   anchor is rewritten when continuity is unavailable, within tolerance, or
277	   excused by a witness.
278	
279	Consequences. An accidental forward wall is accepted only up to 90 d beyond
280	signed evidence, so a wrong write is bounded and heals as signed time catches
281	up; a larger jump writes nothing. Expiry, staleness and future checks still
282	fail closed at tEval. Repeated reboots cannot lower F or freeze payload
283	freshness: F only rises, and freshness is evaluated at tEval ≥ F. Report-only
284	evaluation (doctor) computes the same decision, states and findings, labels
285	`evaluationMode: report-only`, and returns `writes: []` with every write field
286	null; it cannot create a recovery challenge.
287	
288	### S4.5 Recovery of an already poisoned floor
289	
290	A floor years ahead of real time (written by the superseded rule, or by a
291	restore) cannot be lowered by ordinary payloads: tEval ≥ F keeps every document
292	expired. Recovery is an authenticated, install-bound, single-use act:
293	
294	1. `opensip trust recovery-challenge` (decision mode only; global fence, no
295	   project lease) writes one pending challenge and exports
296	   `trust-recovery-challenge.v1.json` (`TrustRecoveryChallengeV1`): a fresh
297	   32-byte host-CSPRNG nonce, `createdWall`, and `recordDigest` =
298	   metadata-profile digest, domain `opensip.metadata.recovery-challenge.1`,
299	   over the six bound fields `{evalHighWater, lastAccepted, rootVersion,
300	   revocationVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, recoveryEpochSerial}`. The
301	   pending record additionally binds `{bootId, createdMono, expiresMono =
302	   createdMono + 24 h, createdWall}` with sleep-inclusive monotonic time. A
303	   new challenge replaces the pending one; a reboot invalidates it.
304	2. The publisher's recovery service (consented online) or the air-gap ceremony
305	   returns `trust-recovery-epoch.v1.json`: an `opensip-signature-envelope.2`
306	   of kind `trust-recovery-epoch` (digest domain
307	   `opensip.metadata.recovery-epoch.1`) with body `TrustRecoveryEpochV1`
308	   `{recoverySchema:1, kind, epochSerial, issuedAt, challenge{nonce,
309	   recordDigest}, counters{rootVersion, revocationVersion,
310	   indexSnapshotVersion}, installBinding:"challenge"}`. Authority is the
311	   **accepted root's `recoveryAuthority.keys` at `recoveryAuthority.threshold`**
312	   (the existing schema-1 field: 5–16 keys, threshold ≥ 3, disjoint from
313	   `rootKeys`), revoked keys excluded. Root keys never count, so routine
314	   recovery never exercises root keys and root-key compromise alone cannot
315	   lower a floor. The accepted root's expiry is not consulted for this one
316	   document because the floor under repair is what expired it. This is the
317	   only external artifact needed.
318	3. `opensip trust recovery-import` verifies, under the global fence and no
319	   project lease, in this order: (a) **strict closed shape of the epoch and of
320	   the pending record before any comparison** (exact-typed constants: `true`
321	   is never `1`, integers are never booleans, timestamps by grammar, hex by
322	   grammar); (b) recovery-authority threshold; (c) a pending challenge exists,
323	   its `bootId` equals the current boot, and `createdMono ≤ mono ≤
324	   expiresMono` (`CHALLENGE_BOOT_CHANGED`, `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`,
325	   `CHALLENGE_CONTINUITY_MALFORMED`); (d) nonce equals the pending nonce;
326	   `recordDigest` equals both the pending value and a fresh digest of the
327	   current record; `epochSerial` > `recoveryEpochSerial`; (e) **every counter
328	   equals the challenged record's counter exactly** (`COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`).
329	   A higher signed counter is refused with that typed detail; the remedy is to
330	   import the ordinary payload that carries it and re-challenge. Nothing is
331	   silently discarded and nothing is silently advanced. (f) `issuedAt` ≥ L and
332	   |`issuedAt` − W| ≤ 24 h (`ISSUED_IN_FUTURE`, `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`).
333	   Any failure refuses `RECOVERY.REFUSED` with the typed detail and changes
334	   nothing.
335	4. On success: F := L := `issuedAt`; anchor cleared; `recoveryEpochSerial` :=
336	   `epochSerial`; pending challenge consumed; audit record `RECOVERY-EPOCH`
337	   with the previous floor. Counters, revocation entries, role states,
338	   journals and namespaces are untouched; no namespace is deleted.
339	
340	Threat statement. The wall is untrusted. The single-boot, 24 h monotonic
341	challenge window plus the ±24 h issue skew mean that no response to an old
342	challenge, held indefinitely, can later lower the floor to a stale real time:
343	after a reboot or after the window the response is dead, and inside the window
344	the signed time must sit within a day of the wall the operator is looking at.
345	This bounds a signed epoch relative to the wall; it does not prove the wall.
346	The protocol promises install binding (nonce + record digest), single use,
347	serial monotonicity, exact counter preservation and no floor below L. It makes
348	**no promise against a malicious publisher**: a recovery authority that signs a
349	false time is outside the protocol, exactly as it is for every other signed
350	time in this contract. Why this cannot revive revoked trust: revocation is by
351	counter and entries, which the epoch may not change; a key revoked before the
352	epoch cannot sign it; expiry is re-evaluated at signed real time, which is ≥
353	every earlier signed time, so a document genuinely expired at real time stays
354	expired. If the recovery authority is unavailable, recovery is impossible and
355	the install must be re-established by fresh install or authenticated adoption.
356	Migration and rollback (S9) never carry a pending challenge; the serial moves
357	forward with the other floors.

359	## S5. Root chain through expired roots (AR-05)
360	
361	An install holding accepted root N evaluates a chain N+1..M link by link. Each
362	link needs the previous root's threshold from that root's keys (continuity)
363	**and** the new root's threshold from its own keys (possession), revoked keys
364	excluded from both. Semantic admission per link: reader supports the schema;
365	version and previous-version contiguity; not issued before its predecessor;
366	issue before expiry; root key policy. Intermediate expiry is never consulted;
367	the final root must be unexpired at tEval and not issued more than 24 h after
368	the wall. Any refusal leaves state unchanged and names the link. Success
369	advances the root counter to M and L to the final root's issue time. An expired
370	root with no chain refuses `ROOT.EXPIRED_NO_CHAIN` with the remedy of presenting
371	a payload carrying N+1..newest. Schema-1 readers refuse a schema-2 root as
372	`ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (typed, not corruption, state unchanged).
373	
374	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
375	
376	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
377	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
378	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
379	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
380	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
381	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
382	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
383	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
384	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
385	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
386	stops before any further effect.
387	
388	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
389	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
390	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
391	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
392	
393	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
394	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
395	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
396	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
397	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
398	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
399	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
400	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
401	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
402	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
403	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
404	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
405	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
406	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.
